  (`https://tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png`) and Esri World Imagery satellite
  (`.../World_Imagery/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}` — note the `{z}/{y}/{x}` ordering, which
  differs from OSM's `{z}/{x}/{y}`). The `TileLayer` carries `key: ValueKey(_sat)` to force a
  full rebuild on toggle.
- Tiles come from `CachedTileProvider` (§14), so previously-downloaded tiles render offline.
- Camera: `initialCenter: LatLng(16.5, 80.6)` (Andhra Pradesh), `initialZoom: 7`. `_fit()`
  auto-fits to all tower coordinates **once** — guarded by `_fitted`, because, as the comment
  says, "Later reloads (a sync, or a return from the inspection form) must not yank the
  camera away from the tower the engineer is standing at." A single tower gets `move(pt, 14)`
  instead of a degenerate `fitCamera`. `_pending`/`_mapReady`/`addPostFrameCallback` exist
  because `MapController` throws if used before `onMapReady`.
- `_zoomBy(±1)` clamps to `[3.0, 19.0]` — "the range both tile sets actually serve".
- `_locate()` takes a one-shot `LocationService.currentFix()`, drops a `MyLocationDot`, and
  moves to zoom ≥15 without zooming *out* if already closer. `LocationUnavailable` becomes a
  snackbar.

**Tower tap** (`_showTower`, `home_tab.dart:171-234`): a modal bottom sheet with the tower
number + criticality chip, type / line / voltage / subdivision / lat-long rows, and a
sentence that reads either "Not yet inspected. Tap Inspect while you are at the tower to
record one." or "Latest inspection: <label>." Buttons: Close and Inspect. The sheet
`Navigator.pop(ctx, 'inspect')` rather than launching from inside its builder — the comment
explains this is so the form is pushed onto the *tab's* navigator once the sheet is gone.
Then `launchInspection(...)` (13.8.2) and, if it returns true, `_load()` to recolour.

**Empty state**: when not loading, no error, and no tower has coordinates, a 94 %-opaque
overlay shows either "No lines assigned to you yet" or "Your towers have no recorded
coordinates" with a matching subtitle. It is stacked *under* the controls so "Offline area"
stays reachable.

**"Download my area"** (`_downloadOffline` → `_OfflineDownloadDialog`,
`home_tab.dart:455-551`): a barrier-dismissible-false `AlertDialog` driving
`OfflineDownloader.instance.downloadJurisdiction(onProgress:)` (§14). It renders
`DownloadProgress.phase` as: `lines` → "Fetching your lines…", `towers` → "Towers d/t…",
`catalog` → "Saving the checklist…", `tiles` → "Map tiles d/t · N MB", default →
"Finishing…". The progress bar is determinate only during the `tiles` phase. Cancel calls
`OfflineDownloader.instance.cancel()`. The blurb states the contract plainly: "Saves your
lines, their towers, the checklist and the map for your jurisdiction so inspection works with
no signal."

**Live refresh**: `initState` adds `_reload` as a listener on `SyncEngine.instance.dataRevision`,
so when a queued inspection finally uploads the map recolours itself.

**FINDING — the tower colour is the *oldest* inspection, not the worst or the newest.**
`home_tab.dart:96-100` builds the colour map with a plain overwrite:

```dart
for (final list in inspLists) {
  for (final s in list) {
    worst[s.towerId] = s.worst;
  }
}
```

`GET /line-inspections/list/` is ordered `-saved_at` (`line_inspection/api/views.py:662`),
i.e. newest first, so for a tower inspected more than once the **last** iterated summary —
the oldest inspection — wins. The variable is named `_worst` and the bottom sheet labels it
"Latest inspection", but it is neither. Contrast `inspections_tab.dart:239-243`, which does
the same job correctly with `worstOf([prev, s.worst])`.

#### 13.8.2 Inspect — `lib/screens/li_tabs/inspection_tab.dart` (291 lines) and the presence gate

*(291 lines as checked out.)* Supervisors and admins
only (13.7).

**What the user sees.** A 240 px map centred on the device at zoom 17, with a scrollable
list of nearby towers below it, nearest first, each showing its distance in metres and either
"In range" (green) or "Override".

**Radii.** Two constants, and the distinction is the whole design:

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `InspectionTab.presenceRadiusM` = `kPresenceRadiusM` | **50 m** | "In range" — the form opens with no questions asked. Defined once in `lib/widgets/inspect_launcher.dart:12` and re-exported by the tab so both entry points cannot drift. |
| `InspectionTab.browseRadiusM` | **500 m** | The list/marker cut-off. Towers farther than this are hidden entirely — otherwise the list would be every tower on every assigned line. |

**GPS lifecycle** (`_startGps`, `inspection_tab.dart:97-129`): `LocationService.ensureReady()`
→ one `currentFix()` for an immediate answer → subscribe to `positionStream()` (best accuracy,
5 m distance filter). Each fix updates `_me`/`_accuracy` and clears `_gpsError`. The map is
auto-centred **only on the first fix** (`_mapCentered`), so it does not fight the user's
panning. Errors render a dismissible amber banner with a Retry button rather than blocking
the tab. The subscription is cancelled in `dispose`.

**Tower data** is loaded exactly like Home (assigned lines → towers), filtered to towers that
actually have coordinates, and is cache-through so the tab works with no signal once the area
is downloaded. `_nearby()` recomputes distances with `LocationService.distanceTo` on every
build and sorts ascending.

**Markers**: green with an accent ring for in-range towers, grey otherwise. Note this map is
a plain `TileLayer` with the **default** tile provider — unlike Home it does *not* use
`CachedTileProvider`, so its tiles are not served from the offline pin cache.

**The audited override** — `lib/widgets/inspect_launcher.dart`. This is the shared gate for
both entry points; its doc comment states the principle: "Being physically at the tower is the
utmost criterion, so the gate is enforced before the form appears… field GPS drifts, so the
override keeps work unblocked while flagging it for oversight."

`launchInspection(context, {tower, inspectorEmployeeId, fix, accuracyM})`:

1. If the caller supplied no `fix` (the Home path — "so it needn't hold the GPS open"), show
   the blocking `_PresenceFixDialog` ("Confirming you are at the tower…"), which takes a
   one-shot `LocationService.currentFix()` and pops a `_PresenceFix{fix, accuracy, error}`.
2. Compute `distance = LocationService.distanceTo(me, tower.lat, tower.lng)`, `null` when
   either the fix or the tower coordinates are missing.
3. Derive `presenceFlag`:

| Condition | `presenceFlag` | Override reason |
|---|---|---|
| `distance != null && distance <= 50` | `'in_range'` | `''` |
| fix obtained, but >50 m or the tower has no coordinates | `'out_of_range'` | **required** |
| no fix at all | `'no_fix'` | **required** |

4. For the two override cases, `askPresenceOverride()` shows a dialog headed by the specific
   problem — the GPS error text for `no_fix`, "This tower has no recorded location" when the
   tower lacks coordinates, or "You are N m from this tower" — followed by: "Inspection is
   meant to be done at the tower (within 50 m). You can continue, but the reason is recorded
   and the inspection is flagged for review." The Continue button **silently does nothing**
   while the reason field is blank (`if (r.isEmpty) return;`), so the reason is genuinely
   mandatory; Cancel aborts the whole launch (`return false`).
5. `LineInspectionApi.loadCatalog()` (cache-through), then push `LineInspectionFormScreen`
   with `inspectorLat`, `inspectorLng`, `gpsAccuracyM`, `presenceFlag`, `overrideReason`.
6. Returns `true` once the form has been opened and closed, so callers know to refresh.
   A catalog failure becomes a "Could not open form: …" snackbar and `false`.

**A hole in the gate.** The History tab's `_inspectTower()`
(`inspections_tab.dart:321-350`) opens `LineInspectionFormScreen` **directly**, bypassing
`launchInspection` entirely. The form's defaults then apply — `presenceFlag: 'in_range'`,
no `inspectorLat/Lng`, no reason — so an inspection created from the History tab's "to be
inspected" chips is submitted claiming in-range presence with no GPS evidence at all. The
server-side gate re-checks distance only for GPS-aware submits (the README notes the "legacy
JSON path" is exempt), so this path is not caught there either.

#### 13.8.3 Tickets — `lib/screens/li_tabs/tickets_tab.dart` (263 lines)

A **defect ticket** is auto-raised by the backend for every defect entry in a submitted
inspection (one ticket per entry), and is the unit of follow-up maintenance work.

**What the user sees.** A row of three `ChoiceChip` filters — `Open` (default), `Closed`,
`All` — over a `RefreshIndicator` list of cards. Each card shows the line name, `T-<tower>`,
the checklist item label with the position in parentheses, the defect label, the follow-up
answers rendered as `v1 · v2 · v3` (`answersText`), then a criticality chip, a status pill and
the raised-at timestamp. Open tickets get a "Close" outlined button.

**Data** (`_load`): `LineInspectionApi.loadTickets(status: _statusFilter, subdivision:
session.scopeSubdivisionId)` → `GET /tickets/?status=&subdivision=`. Then, client-side:

```dart
// Scope strictly to tickets this person raised — the backend has no
// raised-by filter, so narrow it client-side by employee ID.
final mine = tickets.where((t) => t.raisedBy == widget.session.employeeId).toList();
```

This is a real limitation worth knowing: the server returns every ticket visible in the
user's oversight scope, the app downloads them all and then throws most away. For a
supervisor over a large jurisdiction this is wasted payload, and it means the tab is
"tickets I raised", not "tickets in my area".

**Closing a ticket** (`_closeTicket`): a dialog pre-filled with "Attended and rectified"
(and re-applied as the fallback when the user clears it), then
`OfflineActions.closeTicket(ticketId, closedBy, note)` — routed through the outbox, so the
snackbar reads either "Ticket closed" or "Ticket closed offline — will sync when online"
depending on `result.queued`. Then a silent reload.

`initState` subscribes `_onSynced` to `SyncEngine.instance.dataRevision` so a queued close
that later syncs refreshes the list "to reflect the now-authoritative server state".

#### 13.8.4 History — `lib/screens/li_tabs/inspections_tab.dart` (848 lines)

Note the name: the class is `InspectionsTab` but the tab is labelled **History**, and roughly
half the file is the inspection *detail* screen it pushes.

Its purpose: **one flat list of every inspection saved at the viewer's level**, newest first,
grouped by the day the work was done. No line picker, no search, and no forward-looking work.

**Why there is nothing to search.** The tab reads `GET /line-inspections/list/`, which
`_mobile_inspection_scope` (`api/views.py`) has already scoped to the viewer's oversight, so the
response *is* the list to show. An inspector should never have to name a line to reach the
record, and a query could only ever narrow a list the server had already decided they may see.
The earlier design — a debounced line search, a `_allComplete` guard against the
`MAX_LIST` = 500 cap and a per-line drilldown — is gone with it.

**Scope is the level, not the employee — and this was a bug.** The tab first shipped reading
`?inspector=<me>` and filtering again on `s.inspector == _employeeId`. That is wrong for the
same reason it was wrong on the Tickets tab: `inspector_employee_id` records who *captured* an
inspection, and supervisors do not capture — their subordinates do. So a DEE, EE or SE saw an
empty or short History while Home's KPI strip counted the very same inspections, and the two
tabs openly disagreed. `?inspector` remains available on the endpoint (now `__iexact`, so a
difference in case cannot silently return nothing) but the tab does not send it.

A `_ScopeChip` pair — **All at my level** / **Captured by me**, each carrying its own count —
narrows the list on the device. It never touches the coverage figures on the card, which always
describe the whole level.

**The two tabs cannot disagree any more.** Both read the dashboard through the same cache-first
`readDashboard()`, so they share one cached rollup rather than each forcing a fetch (which used
to let them show different totals seconds apart), and the card prints the server's own
`inspected`, `tower_total` and `coverage_pct` — the same three numbers as Home's strip, down to
the rounding.

**Why "to be inspected" is not here.** Towers still awaiting an inspection are forward work,
not history, and Home already owns that job: it maps the assigned lines, ranks the nearest
towers off the live GPS fix, and opens the form through the presence gate. Listing them here
made the tab two products in one, and the chips were a second, gate-thin entry into the form.

**The load** (`_load`): two cache-first reads, not the old `1 + 2N` per-line fan-out.

```dart
final historyRead  = LineInspectionApi.readInspections(force: force);
final coverageRead = LineInspectionApi.readDashboard(force: force);
unawaited(_applyCoverage(coverageRead, token));   // lands independently
```

Each read hands back the cached copy immediately and revalidates behind it, so the list paints
from disk on a tab switch. The two leave together and land independently, so neither waits on the
other, and a failed rollup costs only the meter — "a failure there must not cost the user their
history". A guard token `_token` is compared after every await so a stale reload cannot overwrite
newer state; `force: true` (pull-to-refresh, or a sync landing) goes past the freshness window.

**Grouping** (`groupHistoryByDay`, `@visibleForTesting`): rows are sorted by inspection *date*
descending, ties keeping arrival order (the server sorts by save time, so the last thing saved
that day stays on top). Grouping on the date rather than trusting arrival order is what stops a
backdated inspection — saved days after the visit — from landing among another day's rows and
splitting that day's group in two. `historyDayLabel` renders each group as `TODAY`,
`YESTERDAY` or `24 JUL 2026`.

The body is a `RefreshIndicator` + `CustomScrollView` of:

| Block | Content |
|---|---|
| Summary card | Gradient card: "Coverage at your level", the server's `coverage_pct`, then a three-part 8 px bar (`_CoverageBar`) and the caption "X of Y towers inspected · Z by you". Below a hairline, a scope caption (`ALL AT YOUR LEVEL` / `CAPTURED BY YOU`) over the figures for whichever set the list is showing — Inspections / Defects found / Critical (red once non-zero), plus Pending when anything is still in the outbox. The meter is omitted entirely when the rollup has never loaded; the figures come from the history itself and always show. |
| `_CoverageBar` + `coverageSplit` | The bar carries both readings at once: dark = towers this user inspected, mid = towers their colleagues at the same level inspected, track = untouched. `coverageSplit` reconciles the two sources — the server rollup and the user's own rows — and caps `mine` at `inspected`, because an inspection still in the outbox is in the user's rows but not yet in the rollup and would otherwise draw a "by you" segment longer than the inspected segment containing it. Flex takes the counts directly, so the three parts are exact and always sum to the total. Coverage counts **towers**, not inspections, so re-inspecting one tower cannot push the bar past real coverage. |
| `SliverPersistentHeader(pinned)` per day | `_DayHeaderDelegate`: 34 px, opaque `kSurface` so rows scroll out of sight behind it, day label left and that day's row count right. Its bottom hairline appears only while content is scrolling under it (`overlapsContent`), so a header at rest stays flat. |
| `SliverList` per day | One `InspectionHistoryTile` per inspection. |

**The row** (`InspectionHistoryTile`, public for testing): a 4 px full-height criticality edge,
then `T-<num>` in the scanning position with the line name beside it (a level's history spans
lines), then a meta line of `<criticality word> · <n> defects · <type>`. Criticality is carried
by the coloured edge **and** the word, never colour alone. `defectsLabel` writes
`No defects` / `1 defect` / `4 defects` rather than `n defect(s)`. A negative id means the
inspection is still in the outbox, which shows as an amber `Pending` pill. When `isMine` is false
the capturing employee's id takes the tower type's slot rather than widening the row — on a list
that spans a whole level, who did it outranks the structure type. Rows are lazily built per day
group, so a 500-row history costs nothing up front.

`test/history_grouping_test.dart` covers the grouping rules, the day labels, the defect wording,
`coverageSplit`'s reconciliation (including the unsynced-row cap), and the row's layout on a
360 dp phone with the worst real-world content.

**Photo refs.** Resolution happens at render time in `_liThumb`:

```dart
Widget _liThumb(String ref, {double size = 120}) {
  if (ref.startsWith('local://')) {
    return LiPhotoThumbnail.file(File(ref.substring(8)), size: size);
  }
  return LiPhotoThumbnail.network(LineInspectionApi.mediaUrl(ref), size: size);
}
```

The `local://<abs-path>` scheme is how an optimistically-inserted, not-yet-synced inspection
shows its own photos: the outbox stages the picked image into durable storage and records the
path, so the detail screen can display it from disk long before the server has ever seen it.
Anything else is a server media path resolved by `LineInspectionApi.mediaUrl()` (strip the
trailing `/api` from the base, append `/media/<path>`).

**Detail screen** (`_InspectionDetailScreen` + `_DetailBody`, private to this file): a
`FutureBuilder` over `loadInspectionDetail(id)`. Header card: `T-<num> · <type>`, criticality
chip, line name, `<date> · <inspector>`, and italic remarks when present. Body: **only items
with entries are shown** (`where((r) => r.entries.isNotEmpty)`) — the exception-based
philosophy carried through to reading, since listing 60 "normal" rows would bury the three
that matter. When there are none, a green "All normal". Each `_ItemCard` shows
`<sno>. <label> · <position>`, the item photo if any, then one `_EntryTile` per defect, tinted
6 % with that entry's criticality colour and outlined at 25 %: criticality chip, defect label,
answers line, italic note, and the defect photo.

`_onSynced` (subscribed to `SyncEngine.instance.dataRevision`) reloads the list "so its row
switches from the optimistic (pending) copy to the authoritative server record".

**Offline saves land here immediately.** `OfflineActions._insertOptimisticSummary` writes the
new row into *both* the per-line cache key the Home map reads and the inspector-scoped key this
tab reads (`_summaryKeys`) — the tab no longer reads any per-line list, so writing only that one
would have hidden a no-signal save until it synced. `LiCacheKeys.inspections` appends its
`_by_<id>` segment only when an inspector is given, so every pre-existing cache file on an
installed app keeps its old name and stays readable across the upgrade.

#### 13.8.5 Help — `lib/screens/li_tabs/support_tab.dart` (348 lines)

**What the user sees.** A "Raise a request" card at the top, then a list of existing requests.

**The form**: a category dropdown with exactly four options — `Tower / line data correction`,
`Questionnaire change request`, `Defect ticket dispute`, `Other` — plus Subject and a 3-line
Description, and a "Send to admin" button. Both text fields are mandatory client-side.
Submission goes through `OfflineActions.createSupport(raisedBy, category, subject, text,
subdivisionId, subdivisionName, scopeSubdivisionId)`, so the snackbar is either "Request sent
to admin." or "Saved offline — will send to admin when online." On success the form resets to
its initial state.

The four categories are the deliberate design point: an inspector who finds wrong tower data,
a missing checklist item, or a ticket they disagree with has **no** ability to edit any of
those things in the app — the correction has to be requested from the admin, which keeps a
paper trail and keeps the catalog and asset registry under central control.

**The list**: `loadSupportRequests(subdivision: session.scopeSubdivisionId)`. Each card shows
the subject, a status pill (`open`/`resolved`), the category, the body text, then — if the
admin has responded — a blue-tinted panel reading "Admin: <response>", then the created
timestamp and "by <employeeId>". Management/admin users additionally get a **Resolve** button
on open requests, which demands a non-empty response ("Enter a response before resolving.")
and calls `OfflineActions.resolveSupport(supportId, resolvedBy, response)` — also
outbox-routed. Subscribed to `dataRevision` like the other tabs.

### 13.9 `LineInspectionFormScreen` — `lib/screens/line_inspection_form_screen.dart` (1,126 lines)

The single largest file in the app, and the point of the whole product. Its own summary
(`line_inspection_form_screen.dart:15-19`): "The adaptive tower-inspection form — a Flutter
port of the POC's `Inspect` engine. Exception-based: every applicable item starts Normal; the
inspector marks only defects. The defect editor is adaptive — the chosen defect decides which
follow-up questions appear, and the criticality is suggested from the answers (overridable)
via the server's declarative rules."

**STALE COMMENT — flag.** The very next line (`:21-22`) says "Photos are captured in a later
increment; this build records the full questionnaire structure and saves it to the `clear`
schema." That is no longer true: this same file implements item-level *and* per-defect photo
capture (`_pickPhoto`, `_photoControl`, `_regPhoto`, `_photoUploads`). The comment predates
the photo work and was never removed.

#### Constructor parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tower` | `LiTower` | required | Subject of the inspection; supplies `id`, `towerNumber`, `towerType` (drives N/A gating) and `lineName`. |
| `catalog` | `InspectionCatalog` | required | The **entire** questionnaire. Fetched by the caller (never by the form) so the form is synchronous and testable. |
| `inspectorEmployeeId` | `String` | required | Stamped on the submission. |
| `inspectorLat` / `inspectorLng` | `double?` | `null` | GPS proof of presence. |
| `gpsAccuracyM` | `double?` | `null` | Reported accuracy of that fix. |
| `presenceFlag` | `String` | `'in_range'` | `'in_range' \| 'out_of_range' \| 'no_fix'`. |
| `overrideReason` | `String` | `''` | Required non-empty unless `in_range` — enforced by `launchInspection`, **not** by the form. |

#### The form is 100 % catalog-driven

Nothing about the questionnaire is hardcoded. `build()` is literally
`[_metaCard, for (final g in _cat.groups) _groupCard(g), _remarksCard]`. The nesting mirrors
the catalog model exactly:

```
InspectionCatalog(version, groups[], followUps{key→FollowUpQuestion}, criticalityRules[])
  └─ ChecklistGroup(key, label, sortOrder, items[])              → a collapsible Card
       └─ ChecklistItem(id, key, sno, label, positions[], posMeta,
                        isAvailabilityGated, isPositionAvailabilityGated,
                        applicableTowerTypes[], naReason, groupKey, defects[])
            │                                                    → one bordered row
            ├─ positions[] (e.g. Top / Middle / Bottom)          → one sub-row each
            │    └─ posMeta dropdown (e.g. "Type of insulator")
            └─ Defect(id, key, label, sortOrder, ask[], defaultCriticality)
                                                                 → a ChoiceChip
                 └─ ask[] → followUps[key] → FollowUpQuestion(answerType, options,
                                                              unit, placeholder)
                                                                 → chips / field
                      └─ CriticalityRule(defectKey, followUpKey, operator,
                                         thresholdValue, resultingCriticality, priority)
                                                                 → the suggestion
```

The rationale is recorded in `inspection_catalog.dart:5-8`: "Everything the adaptive
inspection form renders … comes from here rather than being hardcoded, because the server
catalog evolves independently of the app." A new checklist item, defect, follow-up or
criticality rule seeded server-side appears in the field app with **no app release** — which
matters enormously when the users are hundreds of field staff on unmanaged Android phones.

#### Draft state — `lib/models/inspection_draft.dart`

Three classes, ported from the POC's `Inspect.cur`:

| Class | Fields |
|---|---|
| `ItemDraft` | `item` (`ChecklistItem`), `main` (`SlotDraft`), `positions` (`Map<String, SlotDraft>`), `photo` (`File?`, item-level, mutable). Getters: `isPositional` (= `item.hasPositions`), `allEntries` (a `sync*` generator yielding every committed entry across positions, or `main`'s for a plain item). |
| `SlotDraft` | A **slot** = either a whole non-positional item or one position of a positional item. `status` (`normal \| defect \| na \| not_provided`), `entries` (committed `DefectEntryDraft`s), `meta` (`Map<String,String>` for the pos_meta select). Then transient editor state: `editing`, `draftDefectId`, `draftAnswers`, `draftCriticality`, `draftNote`, `draftPhoto`, plus `resetDraft()` which clears all six. |
| `DefectEntryDraft` | `defectId`, `defectKey`, `answers` (`Map<String,dynamic>`), `criticality`, `suggestedCriticality`, `note`, `photo` (`File?`). |

Separating *committed* entries from *draft* editor state is what makes "add another defect to
the same slot" work: the draft is a scratchpad that gets copied into `entries` on commit and
then wiped.

#### Initial state — `_buildDrafts()` (`:74-97`)

For every item in `catalog.allItems`:

```
applies = CriticalityEngine.itemApplies(item, tower.towerType)
main.status = !applies            ? 'na'
            : isAvailabilityGated ? 'not_provided'
            :                       'normal'
for each position p:
  positions[p].status = isPositionAvailabilityGated ? 'not_provided' : 'normal'
  if (posMeta != null) positions[p].meta[posMeta.id] = posMeta.default
```

Three defaults, three different reasons:

- **`normal`** — the exception-based core. The inspector's job is to record deviations, not to
  tick 60 boxes. A tower with nothing wrong is saved by opening the form and pressing Save.
- **`not_provided`** ("Not available") for `is_availability_gated` items — fittings such as
  bird guards or anti-climbing devices that may simply not be installed on a given tower.
  Defaulting these to *Normal* would silently assert that a non-existent fitting is in good
  condition, so the safe default is "not provided" and the inspector must actively say
  "Available" before recording its condition.
- **`na`** — the item does not apply to this tower type at all (see below). Rendered as
  read-only italic text, `'N/A — <naReason or "not applicable">'`.

#### `applicable_tower_types` N/A gating

`CriticalityEngine.itemApplies(item, towerType)`
(`lib/services/criticality_engine.dart:97-112`):

1. Empty `applicableTowerTypes` → applies (the common case).
2. Otherwise **prefix** match, uppercased and trimmed: the catalog gates by family codes
   (`DA`, `DB`, `DC`, `DD`) while real tower types carry a body-extension suffix (`DA+0`,
   `DB+3`), so `'DA+0'.startsWith('DA')` is the whole trick.
3. On no match, the permissive fallback:

```dart
final gateIsDSeries = types.every((c) => c.toUpperCase().startsWith('D'));
final towerIsDSeries = tt.startsWith('D');
if (gateIsDSeries && towerIsDSeries) return false;   // genuinely out of scope → N/A
return true;                                          // outside the gate's family → show it
```

The comment explains the judgement call: a tower that is not in the gated D-series family at
all (`A+0`, `P+0`, `S+0`, `Boom`, …) is treated as **applicable** "so no item is ever silently
un-inspectable on the bulk of real towers". Silently hiding a checklist item is a far worse
failure than showing one that does not apply — the inspector can mark the latter Normal, but
cannot report a defect on something they never saw. The code carries its own caveat: "NOTE:
this gating scheme needs confirmation against APTRANSCO tower nomenclature; it is
intentionally permissive until then."

#### Rendering the status control — `_itemControl()` (`:589-634`)

Five mutually exclusive branches, in order:

| Condition | Rendered control |
|---|---|
| `main.status == 'na'` | Italic `'N/A — <reason>'`. No interaction, no photo control. |
| `hasPositions && isAvailabilityGated` | Two-way segment: **Not available** / **Available**. Available sets `main = 'normal'`, which reveals the position rows. |
| `isAvailabilityGated` (non-positional) | Three-way: **Not available** / **Normal** / **Defect (n)**. |
| `!hasPositions` | Two-way: **Normal** / **Defect (n)**. Note the Normal chip is selected whenever `status != 'defect'`, so it also lights up for any unexpected status. |
| positional, not gated | `SizedBox.shrink()` — "positions carry it". |

The segmented control is hand-rolled (`_seg`/`_segButton`/`_SegOpt`/`_SegTone`) rather than
Material's `SegmentedButton`, so each option can carry its own semantic tone: `ok` → green
14 % tint, `bad` → red 14 %, `np` → grey. The Defect option shows a live count.

An item's row is tinted 6 % `major` orange and outlined in `major` whenever it has any
committed entries, so a scrolled-past group still reads at a glance.

#### Per-position rows — `_posRow()` (`:636-698`)

Each position renders: a 66 px label (`Top`, `Middle`, `Bottom`, …), the optional `pos_meta`
`DropdownButton` (dense, expanded, no underline — e.g. "Type of insulator" with options like
`Fog Disc`, seeded from `posMeta.default`), then its own segmented control (with the
**Not available** option only when `isPositionAvailabilityGated`), then that position's defect
editor when its status is `defect`. Positions are separated by a top hairline.

#### FINDING — marking one position "Not available" wipes every other position

`_setSlotStatus(slot, item, status)` (`:107-131`) contains:

```dart
if (status == 'not_provided' && item.hasPositions) {
  final d = _drafts[item.id]!;
  for (final p in d.positions.values) {
    p.status = item.isPositionAvailabilityGated ? 'not_provided' : 'normal';
    p.entries.clear();
    p.resetDraft();
  }
}
```

The intent (per the comment) is "If a positional item is switched to not_provided/na **at item
level**, clear its positions too." But the guard tests `item.hasPositions`, not "is this the
item-level slot". `_posRow` calls the same function with a **position** slot and the same
`item`, so pressing **Not available** on the `Top` position of a position-gated item also
forces `Middle` and `Bottom` to `not_provided` and silently deletes any defects already
recorded on them. Data loss, no confirmation, no undo.

Related, milder: `_setSlotStatus` clears `slot.entries` on any move away from `defect` — so
tapping Normal on a slot with three recorded defects discards them without asking. And
`_cancelDraft` (`:137-140`) resets a slot with no entries to `'normal'` even if it started
life as `'not_provided'`.

#### The adaptive defect editor — `_defectEditor()` (`:701-868`)

Rendered inline under a slot whose status is `defect`. Sequence:

1. **Committed entries** — one grey card each: criticality chip, `<defect label> — <answers
   joined by " · " with units>` (`_entrySummary`), an × to remove, and an 84 px thumbnail when
   the entry has a photo.
2. **Not editing** → a single `Add defect` / `Add another defect` text button.
3. **Editing** → "What is the problem?" and a `Wrap` of `ChoiceChip`s, one per
   `item.defects`. Choosing a *different* defect clears `draftAnswers` and `draftCriticality`
   (`_chooseDefect`), because the follow-up chain is defect-specific.
4. **One-at-a-time follow-up reveal** (`:786-795`) — the signature interaction:

```dart
var pending = false;
for (final fuKey in def.ask) {
  final fu = _cat.followUps[fuKey];
  if (fu == null) continue;
  children.add(_followUp(slot, fu));
  if (!_isAnswered(slot.draftAnswers[fuKey])) { pending = true; break; }
}
```

Each follow-up in `def.ask` order is rendered, and the loop **stops after the first
unanswered one**. Question 2 does not exist on screen until question 1 has an answer. The
comment calls this "progressive disclosure" and credits the POC; the field rationale is that a
phone screen in sunlight with one gloved hand should show one decision at a time, and that
questions later in a chain are often meaningless before the earlier answers. An unknown
follow-up key is skipped (`continue`) rather than crashing — important, since the catalog can
add keys the app has never seen. `_isAnswered` treats `null`, a blank/whitespace `String` and
an empty `List` as unanswered; any other value counts.

5. **Follow-up widgets** by `answer_type` (`_followUp`, `:870-947`):

| `answerType` | Widget | Stored value | Key |
|---|---|---|---|
| `choice` | `Wrap` of `ChoiceChip`, single-select | `String` | — |
| `multichoice` | `Wrap` of `FilterChip`, toggling in/out of a list | `List<String>` | — |
| `number` | 140 px `TextFormField`, `numberWithOptions(decimal: true)`, with `fu.unit` beside it | `num` via `num.tryParse`, falling back to the raw `String`, or `''` when cleared | `ValueKey('fu_num_<fu.key>')` |
| anything else (`text`) | full-width `TextFormField` with `fu.placeholder` as hint | `String` | `ValueKey('fu_txt_<fu.key>')` |

The `ValueKey`s are load-bearing and the comment says why: "Key by follow-up so switching to a
different defect (which clears `draftAnswers`) also rebuilds this field from scratch —
otherwise Flutter reuses the field's State and leaves the previous defect's typed value
visible while state is empty." Every answer change calls `setState` (so the next follow-up can
reveal) and resets `draftCriticality = null` (so the suggestion re-derives).

6. **Criticality** — only once no follow-up is pending. Header reads
   `Criticality  (suggested: <label>)`, computed live by
   `CriticalityEngine.suggestedCriticality(def, draftAnswers, catalog.criticalityRules)`. Three
   `ChoiceChip`s — **Minor / Major / Critical** only; `ok` is never offerable for a defect —
   pre-selected at the suggestion, tinted 25 % with `critColor(c)`. Tapping one sets an
   explicit `draftCriticality`, i.e. a human override of the rule engine.
7. **Defect photo** — `_photoControl` bound to `slot.draftPhoto`.
8. **Note (optional)** — a `TextFormField` keyed
   `'<identityHashCode(slot)>_<defectId>_note'` so each slot/defect pair keeps its own text.
9. **Save defect / Cancel.**

`_commitEntry` (`:215-249`) re-validates that *every* key in `def.ask` is answered ("Answer the
remaining questions"), recomputes `suggested`, and appends a `DefectEntryDraft` carrying
**both** the human `criticality` (`draftCriticality ?? suggested`) and the machine
`suggestedCriticality` — the divergence between the two is the audit trail of the override.
Then `resetDraft()`.

#### Photos

`_pickPhoto()` (`:184-210`) shows a bottom sheet with **Take photo** (`ImageSource.camera`) and
**Choose from gallery** (`ImageSource.gallery`), then `imageQuality: 85, maxWidth: 1600,
maxHeight: 1600`. `_photoControl` renders either an 84 px `LiPhotoThumbnail.file` with a
remove button, or an outlined "Add photo (optional)" button. It is used in two places:

- **Item-level** (`d.photo`), shown for every item that is not `na`, defective or not.
- **Per-defect** (`slot.draftPhoto` → `entry.photo`), evidence for one specific defect.

#### Remarks

A single free-text `TextFormField` ("Remarks (optional)", 2 lines) in its own card at the
bottom, writing straight to `_remarks` with **no** `setState` — deliberate, since the value is
only read at save time and rebuilding the 1,000-widget tree on every keystroke would be
painful.

#### Save — `_save()` (`:255-319`)

1. **Pre-flight**: collect every slot whose `status == 'defect'` but whose `entries` are
   empty. If any exist, auto-expand the offending groups, toast `'Add defect details for: … —
   or mark Normal'`, and abort. This is the only client-side validation of the whole form.
2. `_buildPayloadItems()` builds `items[]` and, as a side effect, fills `_photoUploads`.
3. `OfflineActions.saveInspection(...)` — see §14 — with `tower`, `inspectorEmployeeId`,
   `catalogVersion: _cat.version`, `date: _todayIso()` (local `YYYY-MM-DD`), `remarks`,
   `clientId`, `items`, `photos: _photoUploads`, `catalog`, `worst: _worstAll()`,
   `defectCount`, and the five GPS fields.
4. Snackbar, differentiated on `result.synced`:
   - online: `'Inspection saved — Tower <n>. <k> defect tickets raised.'`
   - offline: `'Saved offline — Tower <n>. It will upload automatically when you're back online. (<k> defects)'`
5. `Navigator.pop(true)`.

`_clientId = generateUuidV4()` is minted **once** in the state object
(`line_inspection_form_screen.dart:57`, `lib/utils/uuid.dart`). It is the server-side
idempotency key: the same UUID is resent on every outbox retry, so a submit that timed out
after the server had already committed replays to a 200 instead of creating a duplicate
inspection.

#### The `items[]` structure handed to the outbox

`_buildPayloadItems()` (`:321-364`) emits **one row per slot**, i.e. one row per non-positional
item and one row per position of an active positional item:

```jsonc
{
  "item_id": 42,                 // ChecklistItem.id (server resolves by numeric id or slug key)
  "position": "Top",             // "" for non-positional items and for item-level na/not_provided
  "status": "defect",            // normal | defect | na | not_provided
  "meta": {"insType": "Fog Disc"},   // pos_meta selections; {} when none
  "photo_key": "photo_0",        // multipart part name, or null
  "entries": [
    {
      "defect_id": 7,            // Defect.id
      "answers": {"discCount": 2, "side": "LHS"},   // follow-up key → value
      "criticality": "critical",             // what the inspector chose (or accepted)
      "suggested_criticality": "critical",   // what the client's rule engine derived
      "note": "cracked at cap",
      "photo_key": "photo_1"
    }
  ]
}
```

Emission rules:

| Item shape | Rows produced |
|---|---|
| Non-positional | Exactly one: `position: ''`, `meta: main.meta` (always `{}` — meta is only ever seeded on position slots), `entries` from `main`, `photo_key` from the item photo. |
| Positional, item-level `na` or `not_provided` | Exactly one collapsed row: `position: ''`, that status, `meta: {}`, `entries: []`, plus the item photo key. The individual positions are **not** emitted. |
| Positional, active | One row per position, in `item.positions` order, each with its own status/meta/entries. The **item-level photo rides on the first position's row only** (`'photo_key': i == 0 ? _regPhoto(d.photo) : null`), because the server model has one photo field per `ItemResult`. |

`_regPhoto(File?)` (`:379-384`) registers a file under a sequential key `photo_0`, `photo_1`, …
into `_photoUploads` and returns that key; `null` in, `null` out. The counter and the map are
reset at the top of `_buildPayloadItems()`, so a retried build renumbers deterministically.
The outbox then stages each file durably and, at sync time, posts
`multipart/form-data` with one text field `payload` (the JSON above wrapped in
`tower_id / inspector_employee_id / catalog_version / date / remarks / client_id / items[]`
plus the GPS fields) and one file part per `photo_key`.

**N/A and Not-available rows are still transmitted.** Nothing is dropped client-side, so the
server can distinguish "inspected and fine" from "not applicable to this tower type" from
"fitting absent" — which is exactly what coverage reporting needs.

#### The footer

A pinned bar: either an "All normal" green chip, or `worst: <label>` plus "N defects
recorded", and the Save button (spinner + "Saving…" while `_saving`). `_worstAll()` folds
`CriticalityEngine.worstOf` over every committed entry's chosen criticality. Group headers
carry the same idea at group scope: a green `✓` when clean, else a chip reading
"N defects" tinted by that group's worst.

### 13.10 `criticality_engine.dart` vs the server's `services/criticality.py` — divergence report

Both sides implement the same contract: for a defect, walk its `CriticalityRule`s in
ascending `priority`, take the first match, else fall back to `defect.default_criticality`.
Client: `lib/services/criticality_engine.dart:38-84`. Server:
`line_inspection/services/criticality.py:7-45`. Ordering agrees — the client sorts explicitly
(`..sort((a,b) => a.priority.compareTo(b.priority))`), the server relies on
`CriticalityRule.Meta.ordering = ['priority']` (`line_inspection/models.py:378-379`).

**The operator sets do not agree.** The server's authoritative enum is
`CRITICALITY_OPERATOR_CHOICES` (`line_inspection/models.py:356-363`).

| Operator | Server (`criticality.py`) | Client (`criticality_engine.dart`) | Consequence of the mismatch |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gte` | ✅ `_coerce_for_compare` then `>= float(threshold)` | ✅ `_cmp` with `num.tryParse` on both sides | Agree in practice. |
| `lte` | ✅ | ✅ | Agree in practice. |
| `eq` | ✅ Python `==` on the raw values | ✅ but **stringified**: `a.toString() == b.toString()` | **Diverges on type.** Threshold `2` vs answer `"2"`: client matches, server does not. Threshold `2` vs answer `2.0`: both match. |
| `in` | ✅ `value in [threshold…]` | ❌ falls through `default: return false` | **Client never fires the rule** → shows (and sends) the defect's default criticality. |
| `contains_any` | ✅ set intersection with a multichoice answer | ❌ | Same — silently wrong suggestion for any multichoice rule. |
| `contains_all` | ✅ subset test | ❌ | Same. |
| `neq` | ❌ not in the enum, `_rule_matches` returns `False` | ✅ implemented | Client-only. Cannot legally exist in the DB, but if seeded anyway the two sides disagree. |
| `gt` | ❌ | ✅ | Same. |
| `lt` | ❌ | ✅ | Same. |

Two further, subtler divergences:

- **Skip semantics.** Client: `if (!answers.containsKey(r.followUpKey)) continue;` then
  `if (v == null || v == '') continue;` — an **empty-string answer skips the rule**. Server:
  only `if value is None: return False` — an empty string is compared. With `eq` against a
  `''` threshold the server would match where the client skips.
- **Non-numeric threshold on `gte`/`lte`.** Client returns `false` cleanly. Server calls
  `float(threshold)` **outside** the guarded coercion (`criticality.py:24, 27`), so a
  mis-seeded string threshold raises an uncaught `ValueError` during inspection ingest.

**How much this matters today.** The shipped catalog
(`line_inspection/management/commands/seed_checklist_catalog.py`) uses **only** `eq` (always
with string thresholds) and `gte`/`lte` (always with numeric thresholds), so with the current
seed the two engines agree. The divergence is latent: the first `in` / `contains_any` /
`contains_all` rule an admin adds through the web form
(`line_inspection/forms.py:99` exposes `operator` for editing) makes the field app's
suggestion silently wrong.

**Why "silently wrong" is a persisted error, not a cosmetic one.** At ingest,
`line_inspection/api/views.py:522-523`:

```python
suggested = suggest_criticality(defect, answers)
final = entry_data.get('criticality') or suggested
```

The server recomputes `suggested_criticality` itself (good — the audit column is always
server-truth), but the **stored `criticality`, the one that colours the map, sizes the KPI
and is copied onto the auto-raised `DefectTicket`, is the client's value** whenever the client
sends a non-empty one — and the client always does (`_commitEntry` writes `draftCriticality ??
suggested`). So a client-side under-suggestion that the inspector accepts without overriding
is persisted as the ticket's real severity. A `contains_any` rule intended to escalate to
`critical` would file the ticket at the defect's `default_criticality` instead. Any future
change to the operator set must be made in both files, and the safest fix would be for the
server to trust its own `suggested` unless the payload carries an explicit human override
flag.

`worstOf` agrees exactly on both sides — order `none:0, ok:1, minor:2, major:3, critical:4`,
seeded at `'ok'` (`criticality_engine.dart:10-33` vs `criticality.py:48-56`). Note it is
implemented **three** times in the app: `CriticalityEngine.order`/`worstOf`,
`kCritOrder`/`worstOf()` in `lib/utils/li_style.dart:34-51`, and the label maps
`CriticalityEngine.label` vs `kCritLabel` — duplicated constants that could drift.

### 13.11 `location_service.dart` — `lib/services/location_service.dart`

A 68-line static wrapper over `geolocator`. Its framing comment is the important bit: "GPS
works without mobile data, so everything here functions fully offline — only map *tiles* need
a prior download." That is what makes a presence-gated inspection viable in a field with no
signal.

| Member | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `LocationUnavailable(message)` | A plain `Exception` carrying a **user-facing** string; `toString()` returns it verbatim so call sites can put it straight into a snackbar or a banner. Documented as "the `no_fix` presence case (inspection allowed only with an override reason)". |
| `ensureReady()` | (1) `Geolocator.isLocationServiceEnabled()` → throws "Turn on location services (GPS) and try again." (2) `checkPermission()`; if `denied`, `requestPermission()` — the OS prompt is only raised when actually needed. (3) if still `denied` or `deniedForever` → throws "Location permission denied — enable it in Settings." `deniedForever` is *not* distinguished, so the message says "Settings" for both. |
| `currentFix()` | `ensureReady()` then `getCurrentPosition(accuracy: best)`. Any failure is wrapped as `LocationUnavailable('Could not get a GPS fix: $e')` so callers only ever handle one exception type. **No timeout is set**, so on a phone that never gets a lock this can hang until the platform gives up — the `_PresenceFixDialog` is `barrierDismissible: false`, so the user cannot cancel it. |
| `positionStream()` | `getPositionStream(accuracy: best, distanceFilter: 5)` — a new fix only after 5 m of movement, which is the right trade for a walking inspector and saves battery. Does **not** call `ensureReady()`; callers must (the Inspect tab does). "Callers must handle errors (which surface as the no-fix case)." |
| `distanceMeters(lat1, lng1, lat2, lng2)` | `Geolocator.distanceBetween` — haversine, pure computation, no network. Declared but **never called** anywhere in `lib/`. |
| `distanceTo(LatLng from, lat, lng)` | The `LatLng`-flavoured version actually used, by the Inspect tab's `_nearby()` and by `launchInspection`. |

### 13.12 `network_security.dart` — `lib/services/network_security.dart`

**The problem.** The app's default backend is a reserved ngrok HTTPS domain, chosen because
it keeps working over LTE from anywhere. On a corporate network doing TLS interception — an
APTRANSCO FortiGate performing SSL inspection — every HTTPS response is re-signed with the
firewall's own CA, so Dart's `HttpClient` rejects it with `CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED: self
signed certificate` and the app is dead on office Wi-Fi.

`install()` offers **two independent opt-in mechanisms, both off by default**, and is a
complete no-op otherwise — the important property, since it means the shipped build keeps
full, ordinary TLS verification.

1. **Bundled corporate CA (secure).** `rootBundle.loadString('assets/certs/corp_ca.pem')`;
   the content is accepted only if it begins with `-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----`, otherwise
   ignored. When valid, `_CorpHttpOverrides.createHttpClient` starts from
   `SecurityContext(withTrustedRoots: true)` — keeping the built-in roots — and **additively**
   calls `setTrustedCertificatesBytes(bytes)`. Certificates re-signed by that CA then validate
   normally: full authentication, just with one extra trusted root. This is the correct fix.
   The comment records the specific operational detail that cost someone a day: "on this
   project the required CA was `CN=FG6H1FTB22904052, O=Fortinet`; the dev machine only had an
   unrelated `CN=support` Fortinet root, which does not validate the intercepted certs."
2. **Accept the interceptor for the backend host only (insecure).** Enabled with
   `--dart-define=ACCEPT_CORP_MITM=true`. Installs a `badCertificateCallback` that returns
   true **only** when `host == Uri.tryParse(ApiService.baseUrl)?.host` — never a blanket
   accept-all. It still disables TLS authentication for that host, so `install()` prints a
   loud `debugPrint`: "ACCEPT_CORP_MITM is ON — TLS authentication is disabled for the backend
   host. Do not ship this build." The doc comment says the same: "Use only as a last resort on
   a trusted corporate LAN when the CA is unavailable, and never in a build handed to real
   inspectors."

Current state in the checkout: `assets/certs/corp_ca.pem` is an 822-byte instructions file
(first line `# Corporate CA certificate goes here.`) containing no certificate, and
`ACCEPT_CORP_MITM` defaults to false — so `install()` returns immediately at
`network_security.dart:47` and default TLS is in force. The practical workaround in use is the
third one: point the app at the backend over **plain HTTP on the LAN** via the in-app Backend
URL dialog, traffic the firewall never inspects (see 13.14 and the Android
`usesCleartextTraffic` note in 13.17).

### 13.13 Models

#### `lib/models/li_asset.dart`

The `Li` prefix exists to avoid colliding with the deleted legacy `TransmissionLine` /
`TowerLocation` models. Both are immutable with `fromJson` only (the app never uploads an
asset).

`LiLine` — wire keys `id`, `name`, `subdivision_name`, `voltage`, `is_active`:

| Field | Dart type | JSON key | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `int` | `id` | The only non-nullable parse; a missing `id` throws. |
| `name` | `String` | `name` | e.g. `220KV Jammalamadugu- Chakrayapeta DC/SC Line (M)-1`. |
| `voltage` | `String` | `voltage` | `132KV` / `220KV` / `400KV`, as text. |
| `subdivisionName` | `String` | `subdivision_name` | Display only. |
| `isActive` | `bool` | `is_active` (default `true`) | Parsed but **never read** in `lib/`. |

`LiTower` — wire keys `id`, `tower_number`, `tower_type`, `voltage`, `line_name`, `latitude`,
`longitude`, `line_id`, `subdivision_name`:

| Field | Dart type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `int` | Sent as `tower_id` on submit. |
| `towerNumber` | `String` | Displayed as `T-<n>` / "Tower <n>"; not numeric (values like `Boom of MCPM1` exist). |
| `towerType` | `String` | e.g. `DA+0`. **Drives the N/A gating** (13.9). |
| `voltage`, `lineName`, `subdivisionName` | `String` | Display. |
| `latitude`, `longitude` | `double?` | Nullable, and both maps + the presence gate handle null throughout — many towers genuinely have no surveyed coordinates. |
| `lineId` | `int?` | Passed to the outbox for optimistic display. |

#### `lib/models/li_records.dart`

Everything the read/aggregate endpoints return. All immutable, all `fromJson`-only, all
null-tolerant.

| Class | Fields (Dart ← JSON) |
|---|---|
| `Subdivision` | `id`, `name`, `circle`, `division`, `zone`. **Entirely unused** — nothing in `lib/` constructs or renders one. It exists for the `GET /subdivisions/` scope picker that was never built (cf. `LiSession.subdivisionId`). |
| `InspectionSummary` | `id`, `towerId ← tower_id`, `towerNumber`, `towerType`, `lineName`, `date`, `inspector ← inspector_employee_id`, `worst ← worst_criticality` (default `'ok'`), `defectCount ← defect_count`. One row of the History list / the Home colour source. |
| `DefectEntryDetail` | `defectId`, `defectLabel`, `answers` (`Map<String,dynamic>`), `criticality` (default `'minor'`), `note`, `photo` (`String?`). |
| `ItemResultDetail` | `itemId`, `itemLabel`, `sno`, `groupKey`, `position`, `status` (default `'normal'`), `photo` (`String?`), `entries` (`List<DefectEntryDetail>`). |
| `InspectionDetail` | `id`, `towerNumber`, `towerType`, `lineName`, `date`, `inspector`, `remarks`, `worst`, `itemResults`. |
| `TicketRecord` | `id`, `towerId`, `towerNumber`, `lineName`, `itemLabel`, `position`, `defectLabel`, `answers`, `criticality`, `status` (`open`/`closed`), `raisedAt`, `raisedBy ← raised_by_employee_id`, `closedBy`, `closeNote`. Getter `isOpen`. |
| `SupportRequest` | `id`, `raisedBy`, `category`, `subject`, `text`, `status` (`open`/`resolved`), `createdAt`, `response`, `resolvedBy`, `subdivisionId`, `subdivisionName`. Getter `isOpen`. |
| `DashLine` | `lineId`, `name`, `towerCount`, `inspected`, `pct`, `openDefects`. **Unused** — the Home KPI strip reads only the scalar totals. |
| `DashSubdivision` | `id`, `name`, `towerCount`, `inspected`, `open`, `critical`. Commented "empty unless HQ view". **Unused.** |
| `DashboardData` | `towerTotal`, `inspected`, `coveragePct`, `openTotal`, `closedTotal`, `criticality` (`Map<String,int>` defaulting to `{critical:0, major:0, minor:0}`), `byComponent` (`List<MapEntry<String,int>>` from `[{item, count}]`), `lines`, `subdivisions`. Only the first four scalars are rendered; `criticality`, `byComponent`, `lines` and `subdivisions` are parsed and discarded — the app has no charts. |

Note `DashboardData.byComponent` is the one non-defensive parse in the file:
`(e['count'] as num).toInt()` throws if `count` is null, which would fail the whole dashboard
load (caught and ignored by the Home tab, so the KPI strip just shows `—`).

#### `lib/models/inspection_catalog.dart`

Documented in 13.9 as the form's driving structure. Field-level detail:

| Class | Fields | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `FollowUpQuestion` | `id`, `key`, `questionText`, `answerType`, `options`, `unit`, `placeholder` | Getters `isChoice`/`isMultiChoice`/`isNumber`/`isText`. `answerType` defaults to `'text'`, which is also the form's fall-through branch, so an unknown type degrades to a free-text field rather than rendering nothing. |
| `CriticalityRule` | `defectKey`, `followUpKey`, `operator` (default `'eq'`), `thresholdValue` (`dynamic`, straight from jsonb — number, string or list), `resultingCriticality` (default `'minor'`), `priority` | Lives at the **top level** of the catalog and is matched to defects by `defectKey`, mirroring the reshaped server payload. |
| `Defect` | `id`, `key`, `label`, `sortOrder`, `ask` (ordered follow-up keys), `defaultCriticality` (default `'minor'`) | |
| `PosMeta` | `id`, `label`, `defaultValue ← default`, `options` | `static PosMeta? fromJson(Map?)` returns `null` for a null map — a static factory rather than a constructor precisely so it can return null. |
| `ChecklistItem` | `id`, `key`, `sno`, `label`, `sortOrder`, `positions`, `posMeta`, `isAvailabilityGated`, `isPositionAvailabilityGated`, `applicableTowerTypes`, `naReason`, `groupKey`, `defects` | Getters `hasPositions`, `defectByKey(key)`, `defectById(id)` — the form resolves by **id** because that is what the payload carries. |
| `ChecklistGroup` | `id`, `key`, `label`, `sortOrder`, `items` | |
| `InspectionCatalog` | `version`, `groups`, `followUps` (a `Map<String,FollowUpQuestion>` built by key during parse), `criticalityRules` | Getter `allItems` flattens groups "in inspection order". `version` is stamped onto every submission as `catalog_version`, so a stored inspection is always interpretable against the catalog revision that produced it. The header notes the catalog "is version-stamped; the app caches it and only re-parses when the version changes". |

#### `lib/models/inspection_draft.dart`

Covered in 13.9. Referenced only by the form screen. It is the one model file holding
`dart:io` `File`s (the not-yet-uploaded photos) and the one that is mutable.

### 13.14 Widgets

| Widget | File | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `SyncStatusBar` | `lib/widgets/sync_status_bar.dart` (274 lines) | Nested `ValueListenableBuilder`s over `ConnectivityService.instance.online` and `SyncEngine.instance.status`. Five states, evaluated in order: **syncing** (blue, spinner, "Syncing N changes…"), **offline** (amber, "Offline — N changes waiting to sync" or "Offline — showing saved data"), **failed** (red, "N changes didn't sync · M pending", action "Retry"), **pending** (blue, "N changes to upload", action "Sync now"), and **null → `SizedBox.shrink()`** when online and clean. Hiding itself entirely in the normal case is the design point: the strip is only ever noise-free feedback. Tapping opens `_SyncDetailsSheet`, which lists each `OutboxOp` (`op.label`, and "Waiting to upload" / "Waiting to retry (n)" / "Couldn't sync · <lastError>") with a manual **Sync now** button. |
| `LiPhotoThumbnail` | `lib/widgets/li_photo_thumbnail.dart` (193 lines) | Two named constructors, `.network(url)` and `.file(File)`, sharing one implementation via an `ImageProvider` getter — network goes through `CachedNetworkImageProvider` "so a photo viewed once stays viewable offline". Renders a rounded, cover-fit square (default 120 px) with a determinate `loadingBuilder` spinner, a `broken_image_outlined` fallback, and a small dark zoom badge bottom-right so it reads as tappable. Tapping pushes a transparent, `barrierColor: black87` route with a `Hero` + `InteractiveViewer(maxScale: 5)`, dismissible by backdrop tap or an × button. The Hero tag is a **per-instance `UniqueKey()`**, not the URL — the comment explains that URL tags "would collide when the same photo appears more than once on a screen (e.g. an item photo repeated across its defect entries)", which crashes Hero. |
| `TowerDot` / `MyLocationDot` | `lib/widgets/map_dots.dart` (51 lines) | `TowerDot(color, onTap, ring)` — a filled circle with a 2 px white border, or a 3 px `kBrandAccent` ring when `ring: true` (used for in-range towers). "no clustering — the user prefers simple pins" is an explicit product decision recorded in the comment. `MyLocationDot` — an accent dot, 3 px white border, accent glow. |
| `editBackendUrl(context)` | `lib/widgets/backend_url_dialog.dart` (63 lines) | Not a widget class but a `Future<bool>` dialog function. Pre-fills with the current override (blank when none), explains the corporate-Wi-Fi case in the body, shows the compile-time default as reference text, and hints `http://192.168.137.1:8000/api` (a Windows mobile-hotspot address). On Save it calls `ApiService.setBaseUrl(text)` — an empty string clears the override — and returns `true` so the caller can retry whatever failed. Reachable from the login screen ("Change server") and the hub app bar. |
| `launchInspection` / `askPresenceOverride` | `lib/widgets/inspect_launcher.dart` (223 lines) | The presence gate; documented in 13.8.2. |

### 13.15 Theming — `lib/utils/li_theme.dart` and `lib/utils/li_style.dart`

`li_style.dart` (412 lines) holds tokens and shared stateless components; `li_theme.dart`
(318 lines) turns them into a single `ThemeData` so, per its comment, "every screen inherits
one consistent, enterprise-grade visual language instead of styling itself ad hoc". The app is
**light-mode only** (`themeMode: ThemeMode.light`, `main.dart:65`).

#### Criticality colour map — `kCritColor` (`li_style.dart:18-24`)

| Key | Hex | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ok` | `#12A150` | Normal / no defect |
| `minor` | `#E8A100` | Minor |
| `major` | `#EC7A38` | Major |
| `critical` | `#DA3838` | Critical |
| `none` | `#8A8F99` | Not inspected (UI-only pseudo-state) |

Described as "from the POC's validated colours" — i.e. field-tested for readability in
sunlight, not picked fresh. `critColor(c)` falls back to `none`, `critLabel(c)` returns the
key itself when unknown, and `critChip()` always pairs the colour with a **text label** so
status is never conveyed by colour alone (colour-blind safety, and phone screens outdoors).

#### Brand palette

| Token | Hex | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `kBrandPrimary` | `#14243D` | "Deep corporate navy… A muted, serious navy (kept in the AP TRANSCO blue family to sit with the blue logo) rather than a bright primary blue." App bars, filled buttons. |
| `kBrandPrimaryDark` | `#0B1526` | Gradient depth, pressed states, all shadow colours. |
| `kBrandAccent` | `#3D6AA6` | "A restrained steel-blue accent" — meters, links, section-header icons, the location dot. |
| `kBlue`, `kBlue600`, `kBlue100` | = accent, = primary, `#DCEAFB` | Back-compat aliases for POC-era screens; `kBlue100` is a real light tint used by the sync banner and the support-response panel. |
| `kInk` / `kInkSoft` / `kInkFaint` | `#16202E` / `#5A6675` / `#8A93A3` | Primary / secondary / tertiary text. |
| `kSurface` / `kCardBg` / `kOutline` | `#F4F7FB` / `#FFFFFF` / `#E2E8F1` | Scaffold background / cards & sheets / hairlines. |

#### Scales

`kSpaceXs 4 · kSpaceSm 8 · kSpaceMd 12 · kSpaceLg 16 · kSpaceXl 24`;
`kRadiusSm 10 · kRadiusMd 14 · kRadiusLg 18 · kRadiusXl 24 · kRadiusPill 999`.
Elevation is two named shadow lists rather than Material elevations: `kShadowSoft`
(6 % @ 14 blur, y+4) and `kShadowFloating` (12 % @ 20 blur, y+8), both in
`kBrandPrimaryDark`. `kBrandGradient` is a topLeft→bottomRight `kBrandPrimary →
kBrandPrimaryDark` linear gradient, used on the login hero.

#### Shared state helpers (the reason every screen looks the same)

| Helper | What it renders |
|---|---|
| `critChip(crit, {text})` | Pill: 8 px colour dot + label, 12 % fill, 45 % border. |
| `statusPill(status)` | Uppercase `OPEN` (major orange) / anything else (ok green), 12 % fill, 55 % border, letter-spaced. |
| `liSectionHeader(icon, title, {count, trailing})` | Accent icon + 15 px bold title + optional `liCountBadge`. |
| `liCountBadge(count)` | Small accent-tinted count pill. |
| `liEmptyState(icon, title, {subtitle})` | 76 px accent-tinted disc with the icon, centred title, optional supporting line. |
| `liLoading({message})` | **Branded**: `kLogoMark` inside a 60 px 2.6 px accent progress ring, optional caption — "Used in place of a bare spinner so waits feel like part of the product." |
| `liErrorState(message, {onRetry, title})` | 72 px red-tinted disc with `cloud_off_rounded`, title (default "Something went wrong"), the detail line, and an optional Retry `FilledButton` — "so every failure across the tabs reads the same". |
| `liBrandBadge({size, radius})` | White rounded badge holding the tower mark, for placement on the dark gradient. |
| `answersText(Map)` | Joins answer values with ` · `, flattening lists with `, `. |

#### `buildLiTheme()`

`ColorScheme.fromSeed(kBrandPrimary, light)` with `primary`, `secondary`, `surface`,
`onSurface`, `error` (= `kCritColor['critical']`) and `outlineVariant` overridden;
`Typography.blackMountainView` re-weighted and `.apply(fontFamily: 'Roboto')` (no custom font
is bundled, so this is the platform Roboto); `splashFactory: InkSparkle`. It then themes
`appBar` (flat, white, hairline bottom border, `surfaceTintColor: transparent` to kill M3's
scroll tint), `card` (elevation 0 + a real 1 px outline — a flat, outlined card language
rather than shadows), `inputDecoration` (filled white, dense, `kRadiusMd`, accent 1.6 px
focus ring, critical-red error borders), `filled`/`elevated`/`outlined`/`text` buttons,
`chip`, `segmentedButton`, `divider`, `tabBar`, `dialog`, `bottomSheet` (top-rounded
`kRadiusXl`, drag handle on), `snackBar` (floating, `kInk` background), `listTile`,
`dropdownMenu`, `progressIndicator` (accent) and `floatingActionButton`.

One deliberate inconsistency to know about: `tabBarTheme` is white-on-transparent (built for
a dark gradient bar), which is why the hub's bottom `TabBar` overrides `labelColor`,
`unselectedLabelColor` and the indicator locally (13.7).

### 13.16 Dead code and unreferenced files

Method: for each of the 37 files under `lib/`, grep the whole `lib/` + `test/` tree for its
basename excluding its own declaration.

**`lib/screens/line_inspection_entry_screen.dart` (311 lines) — confirmed dead. Zero
references.** No file imports it and no route constructs `LineInspectionEntryScreen`. It is
the pre-authentication entry point: a screen with a free-text "inspector id" field persisted
to a `li_inspector_id` SharedPreferences key, a line search, a Loc-No picker and a Backend-URL
action, opening `LineInspectionFormScreen` with `inspectorEmployeeId: inspector.isEmpty ?
'unknown' : inspector`. Its own doc comment calls it "a slim stand-in for the POC's login +
map/selectors while that flow is being built". `WelcomeScreen` → `LineInspectionLoginScreen`
→ `LineInspectionHubScreen` replaced it wholesale. It still compiles (so `flutter analyze`
stays clean and it is not obviously rotting), and it is the only remaining code path that
would submit an inspection under an unauthenticated free-text identity — worth deleting.

Every other file under `lib/` is reachable from `main.dart`. Unreferenced **members** inside
live files, however, are worth listing since they represent built-but-unwired capability:

| Symbol | File | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Subdivision` | `lib/models/li_records.dart:6` | Never constructed or rendered. |
| `DashLine`, `DashSubdivision` | `lib/models/li_records.dart:271, 298` | Parsed into `DashboardData`, never read. |
| `DashboardData.criticality`, `.byComponent`, `.lines`, `.subdivisions` | same | Parsed, never rendered. |
| `LiSession.copyWith`, `subdivisionId`, `subdivisionName`, `displayName`, `tier`, `LiLine.isActive` | `lib/models/li_session.dart`, `li_asset.dart` | Parsed/persisted, never written or displayed (13.5). |
| `UnauthorizedException` handling | `lib/services/line_inspection_api.dart:18` | Thrown, never caught (13.6). |
| `LocationService.distanceMeters` | `lib/services/location_service.dart:63` | Never called. |
| `liBrandBadge`, `kShadowSoft` | `lib/utils/li_style.dart:141, 103` | Defined, never used. |
| `assets/data/*.json` | pubspec assets | Two dead files, ~600 KB (13.2). |
| `cupertino_icons` | pubspec | No Cupertino widget in the app. |

### 13.17 Platform configuration

The iOS project exists and is complete enough to build (Runner target, `SceneDelegate.swift`,
a generated app-icon set, `RunnerTests.swift`), and `linux/` and `macos/` desktop scaffolds
are present from the Flutter template — but the product is **Android-focused**: the
`applicationId` is committed, the launcher icons and both splash variants are generated for
Android including Android-12 and night-mode drawables, and the one configuration that the
real deployment depends on (cleartext HTTP, below) is Android-only.

#### Android — `android/app/build.gradle.kts`

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| `namespace` / `applicationId` | `com.example.drone_inspection_app` — still the Flutter template default; the file carries the generated `// TODO: Specify your own unique Application ID`. Shipping under `com.example.*` is blocked by Google Play, so this **must** change before any store release (and changing it later is a new app identity). |
| `compileSdk`, `minSdk`, `targetSdk`, `versionCode`, `versionName` | All inherited from the Flutter Gradle plugin (`flutter.compileSdkVersion`, `flutter.minSdkVersion`, `flutter.targetSdkVersion`, `flutter.versionCode`, `flutter.versionName`), i.e. not pinned in the repo — they move with the Flutter SDK on the build machine. `flutter_launcher_icons` separately declares `min_sdk_android: 21`. |
| Java / Kotlin target | `JavaVersion.VERSION_17` for source and target; `JvmTarget.JVM_17`. |
| **Signing** | `release { signingConfig = signingConfigs.getByName("debug") }`, with the generated comment "Signing with the debug keys for now, so `flutter run --release` works." **A release APK built from this tree is signed with the debug keystore** — installable for testing, not publishable, and not upgradeable from a properly-signed build. |
| Plugin versions | `com.android.application` 9.0.1, `org.jetbrains.kotlin.android` 2.3.20, `dev.flutter.flutter-plugin-loader` 1.0.0 (`android/settings.gradle.kts`). |
| Activity class | `com.example.drone_inspection_app.MainActivity` (Kotlin). |

#### Android — `android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`

| Declaration | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `<uses-permission CAMERA>` | required | `image_picker` camera capture in the form. |
| `<uses-permission INTERNET>` | required | All backend traffic + map tiles. |
| `<uses-permission ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION>` | required | Coarse fallback for the presence gate. |
| `<uses-permission ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION>` | required | `LocationAccuracy.best` needs fine location for a 50 m gate to mean anything. No background-location permission is requested — the app only reads position while in use. |
| `android:label` | `Aptransco TIS` | |
| **`android:usesCleartextTraffic="true"`** | **set** | **Load-bearing.** Since Android 9 (API 28) plain HTTP is blocked by default. This flag is what makes the documented corporate-Wi-Fi workaround possible: pointing the Backend URL at `http://<lan-ip>:8000/inspection/api` over the laptop's hotspot, bypassing the FortiGate's TLS interception entirely (13.12, 13.14). It is also a blanket permission — *any* host may be reached over plain HTTP, not just the LAN backend. A `network_security_config.xml` restricting cleartext to specific domains would be the tighter form. |
| `android:largeHeap="true"` | set | Headroom for full-resolution camera bitmaps and a map full of tiles. |
| `android:enableOnBackInvokedCallback="true"` | set | Android 13+ predictive back. |
| Activity | `singleTop`, `taskAffinity=""`, `@style/LaunchTheme`, hardware-accelerated, `adjustResize`, broad `configChanges` | Standard Flutter template. `adjustResize` matters for the form's many text fields. |
| `<queries>` | `ACTION_PROCESS_TEXT` / `text/plain` | Package-visibility declaration required by the Flutter engine's text plugin. |

`geolocator`, `image_picker` and the other plugins contribute their own manifest entries at
merge time, so this file lists only what the app itself declares.

#### iOS — `ios/Runner/Info.plist`

| Key | String |
|---|---|
| `NSCameraUsageDescription` | "This app needs camera access to capture tower inspection images" |
| `NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription` | "This app needs photo library access to attach an existing photo to a tower inspection" |
| `NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription` | "This app uses your location to center the map and show your distance to towers" |

Plus `CFBundleDisplayName`/`CFBundleName` = `Aptransco TIS`, all orientations except
upside-down on iPhone, `CADisableMinimumFrameDurationOnPhone` (ProMotion), and a
`UIApplicationSceneManifest` pointing at `$(PRODUCT_MODULE_NAME).SceneDelegate`.

Two gaps worth noting on iOS. (1) There is **no `NSAppTransportSecurity` exception**, so ATS
blocks plain HTTP — the LAN-over-HTTP fallback that is the app's primary corporate-network
workaround **does not work on iOS at all**, while Android explicitly enables it. (2) There is
no `NSLocationAlwaysAndWhenInUseUsageDescription`, which is correct for this app (it never
needs background location) but means any future background tracking would require a plist
change.

### 13.18 Tests — `test/`

Two files, 33 lines between them. This is a very thin safety net for a 9,300-line app: there
is no test of the criticality engine, the payload builder, the presence gate, the N/A gating
or the outbox.

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| `test/uuid_test.dart` | Two `test`s against `generateUuidV4()`. (a) *"generates well-formed version-4 UUIDs"* — 100 generations, each matched against `^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-4[0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$`, which pins both the version nibble (`4`) and the RFC-4122 variant nibble (`8`/`9`/`a`/`b`). (b) *"does not repeat"* — 1,000 generations collected into a `Set`, asserting `length == 1000`. Both matter because this UUID is the server's idempotency key: a malformed or colliding `client_id` would either be rejected or, worse, cause one inspection to be treated as a replay of another. |
| `test/widget_test.dart` | One `testWidgets`, *"App boots to the line-inspection login screen"*: `pumpWidget(const AptranscoApp()); await tester.pump(); expect(find.byType(MaterialApp), findsOneWidget);`. Note it pumps `AptranscoApp` **directly**, not `main()`, so none of the startup sequence (13.3) runs — no SharedPreferences, no outbox, no connectivity — which is exactly why it can run at all without platform-channel mocks. It also does **not** actually assert that the login screen appears (only that a `MaterialApp` exists), so the test's name over-promises; it is a pure "does the widget tree construct without throwing" smoke test. The single `pump()` does not advance past the 1,100 ms splash. |
