| # | Claim | Where | Reality |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | "Sign-in is still disabled — the hub boots with a default Head-Office session"; "its 'Get Started' continues into the hub" | `lib/main.dart:66-68` | Stale. `WelcomeScreen` is a 1.1 s auto-advancing splash with no button, and it routes to the real checkCred login unless a token is stored (13.3). |
| 2 | "Photos are captured in a later increment" | `lib/screens/line_inspection_form_screen.dart:21-22` | Stale. The same file implements item-level and per-defect camera/gallery capture (13.9). |
| 3 | "401 → re-login"; "The app clears the session and returns the user to the login screen." | `line_inspection/README.md` changelog; `lib/services/line_inspection_api.dart:16-18` | Not implemented. `UnauthorizedException` is thrown but caught nowhere (13.6). |
| 4 | Criticality "mirrors `services/criticality.py`" | `line_inspection/README.md`; `lib/services/criticality_engine.dart:38` | The operator sets differ in both directions: the client lacks `in`/`contains_any`/`contains_all`, the server lacks `neq`/`gt`/`lt`, and `eq` uses different type semantics (13.10). |
| 5 | "No GPS proximity gate"; "No auth today — inspector identity is a free-text string"; tabs "dashboard/inspections/map/register/tickets/support" | `line_inspection/README.md`, "Phase 4 — Flutter field app" section | Describes the **pre-Phase-4 base**, and is contradicted by the same README's own changelog and by the code: there is a hard 50 m gate with audited override, token auth on every request, and the tabs are Home / Inspect / Tickets / History / Help. There is no map tab and no register tab. |
| 6 | "5-tab shell" | `line_inspection/README.md` changelog | Only for management/admin. A field engineer — the primary user — sees **four** tabs; Inspect is hidden (`hub_screen.dart:28`). |
| 7 | Home's tower colour is the "Latest inspection" | `home_tab.dart:96-100, 202` | It is the **oldest** inspection's criticality, because a plain map overwrite runs over a `-saved_at`-ordered list (13.8.1). |
| 8 | Marking one position "Not available" affects only that position | implied by `_posRow` | It resets **all** positions of the item and deletes their recorded defects (13.9). |
| 9 | The presence gate is enforced before the form appears | `lib/widgets/inspect_launcher.dart:14-21` | True for Home and Inspect, but the History tab's `_inspectTower` bypasses `launchInspection` and submits with the default `presence_flag: 'in_range'` and no GPS (13.8.2). |
## 14. Flutter Offline-First Subsystem & API Client

This is the app's defining engineering feature and the part most worth understanding before
changing anything. It is not "a cache bolted on" — offline is the *default assumption*, and the
online path is treated as an optimisation.

**Why.** A field engineer walks a transmission corridor. Towers sit in fields, hills and forest
with no cellular coverage; a patrol can last days between signal. If the app required a network
to record an inspection, it would be useless for its actual job. So every read must survive with
no signal, and every write must be durable the instant the inspector taps Save — before any
network is involved.

Files covered: `lib/services/offline/` (8 files, 1,600 lines), `lib/services/line_inspection_api.dart`
(461 lines), `lib/utils/uuid.dart`, `lib/widgets/sync_status_bar.dart`.

---

### 14.1 The shape of the whole thing

```
                    ┌──────────────── UI (tabs, form screen) ─────────────────┐
                    │                                                          │
        READ PATH   │                                       WRITE PATH         │
            │       │                                            │             │
            ▼       │                                            ▼             │
   LineInspectionApi│                                     OfflineActions       │
   ._readThrough()  │                            (optimistic cache patch       │
            │       │                             + durable enqueue)           │
     online?│       └────────────────────┬───────────────────────┬─────────────┘
        ┌───┴───┐                        │                       │
       yes      no                       ▼                       ▼
        │        │                  LocalStore              OutboxStore
        ▼        ▼               (cache/ media/)          (outbox/, 1 file/op)
    HTTP GET  LocalStore                                        │
        │     .getCache()                                       │  FIFO, durable
        │        │                                              ▼
        ├────────┘                                        SyncEngine._drain()
        ▼                                                       │
   putCache() ──────────────► cache/<key>.json                  ▼
                                                        LineInspectionApi
                                                        (submit / close / …)
                                                                │
                                                                ▼
                                                        Django REST backend
```

Two rules make the whole design work:

1. **Reads are cache-through.** A successful GET is always written to disk. If the network is
   unavailable *or* the request fails, the last cached copy is served instead. Only when there is
   nothing cached does the user see an error.
2. **Writes are queued first, sent second.** An inspection is written to the durable outbox
   *before* any network attempt. A crash, a battery pull, or an OS kill immediately after Save
   cannot lose field work.

**Storage lives under `getApplicationSupportDirectory()`, not the cache directory**
(`local_store.dart:50`). This is deliberate and important: Android may evict the cache directory
under storage pressure. Queued field work and staged photos must not be evictable.

Four directories under `<appSupport>/offline/`:

| Dir | Contents | Evictable? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cache/` | Write-through API responses, one JSON file per cache key | By the app only |
| `outbox/` | Queued changes, one JSON file per op | Never (until synced) |
| `media/` | Photos staged out of the OS picker cache | Never (until synced) |
| `tiles/` | Map tiles; `tiles/pinned/` holds downloaded-region tiles | LRU, except `pinned/` |

Everything is **plain files** — no SQLite, no native DB. Stated rationale
(`local_store.dart:30-32`): it builds unchanged on every platform the app targets. All writes are
atomic (write `.tmp`, then `rename`), so a kill mid-write can never leave a half-written record.

---

### 14.2 `ConnectivityService` — "online" means *the backend answers*

`connectivity_service.dart` (90 lines). A singleton exposing `ValueNotifier<bool> online`.

The critical design point: **link-layer connectivity is not enough.** A phone can sit on
corporate Wi-Fi with full bars and no route to the server — precisely the situation described in
§2.8, where the ngrok host is DNS-sinkholed or TLS-intercepted. So when a link is present, the
service confirms with a cheap probe before declaring online:

```dart
Future<bool> _reachable() async {
  final res = await http.get(Uri.parse('$base/ping/'))
                        .timeout(const Duration(seconds: 6));
  // Any HTTP response — even 404 from an older backend without /ping/ —
  // proves the server is reachable. Only a transport failure means offline.
  return res.statusCode < 500;
}
```

This is why `GET /ping/` exists as an unauthenticated endpoint (§11).

| Member | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `online` | Starts optimistically `true` so the first screen tries the network; the first probe corrects within seconds |
| `init()` | Subscribes to `connectivity_plus` changes; kicks a non-blocking first `refresh()` |
| `_onChange` | No link ⇒ immediately offline. Link present ⇒ re-probe (a link is not proof) |
| `refresh()` | Re-probe now. `_probing` guard prevents concurrent probes |
| `reportFailure()` | Called by any request that fails with a transport error — schedules a re-probe |

`reportFailure()` is the subtle one: a normal request failing is *evidence* about connectivity, so
it feeds back into the shared state and flips the UI to the offline banner. Without it the app
would keep believing it was online and keep stalling on doomed requests.

If the probe itself throws, the last known value is deliberately left in place rather than
guessing.

---

### 14.3 `LocalStore` — the durable file store

`local_store.dart` (179 lines).

**Cache API.** Each entry is a wrapper `{"t": <epoch millis>, "b": "<raw response body>"}` so the
UI can show "updated N minutes ago":

| Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `putCache(key, body)` | Atomic write of a raw response body |
| `getCache(key)` | Body, or `null` on miss **or corrupt entry** (a corrupt file is treated as a miss, not an error) |
| `cacheTime(key)` | When it was cached |
| `removeCache(key)` | Drop one entry |
| `patchCachesWithPrefix(prefix, transform)` | Rewrite every cached body whose key starts with `prefix` |
| `purgeUserData()` | Empty `cache/` and `photos/` — everything belonging to the employee who was signed in |

`patchCachesWithPrefix` is what makes optimistic writes look right everywhere. One resource is
cached under many keys — the ticket list exists separately for each filter combination — so
closing a ticket must patch all of them. The transform returns the body unchanged to skip an
entry.

**Media staging.** `stageMedia(src, name)` copies a photo out of the OS picker's cache into
`media/` and returns the durable path. The queued inspection references the copy, so the photo
survives even if the picker cache is cleared before sync. `deleteMedia(path)` removes it after a
successful sync.

**No cache eviction.** There is no size cap or TTL on `cache/`. Entries are only removed
explicitly. In practice the keyspace is bounded by the user's jurisdiction, so this is fine — but
it is unbounded in principle.

**Sign-out / switching employee — `purgeUserData()`.** Cache keys are per-*resource*, never
per-employee (`li_lines_all`, `li_dash_x`, `li_towers_<id>`), because for most of this app's life
one device meant one engineer. They are still the right keys; what changed is that a second
employee's data must not be sitting in them. `purgeUserData()` empties `cache/` and `photos/` and
is called from `AuthStore.save()` (only when the incoming `employeeId` differs from the stored
one) and unconditionally from `AuthStore.clear()`.

What it deliberately leaves alone, and why:

| Directory | Wiped? | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cache/` | **yes** | Every API response — the whole of the previous employee's jurisdiction |
| `photos/` | **yes** | Their inspection evidence, pulled down for offline viewing (includes `photos/pinned/`) |
| `outbox/` | no | Field work that never reached the server. Scoped by owner instead — see §14.5 |
| `media/` | no | The staged photos those queued ops still need in order to upload |
| `tiles/` | no | Public OSM / ArcGIS base-map imagery. Reveals nothing about a jurisdiction, and re-fetching it would cost the next user a blank map |

> **Fixed — signing in as a second employee showed the first one's data.** Sign-out cleared only
> `li_session_v1` out of SharedPreferences, so every `read*` call answered the new session from the
> previous employee's cache — and because master data is held for `freshMaster` (10 minutes), the
> network was not even consulted to correct it. The wipe is on `AuthStore.save()` as well as
> `clear()` on purpose: the cases that actually happen in the field are the app being force-killed
> instead of signed out, a session left behind by a crash, and a second person signing in on a
> shared device — none of which run the sign-out path. Two narrower holes were closed with it:
> `LineInspectionApi._inFlight` is now keyed by token + cache key (a GET started under one employee
> can no longer be handed to a screen asking as another), and `_revalidate` re-checks the token
> before `putCache`, so a response in flight across the switch cannot write the old employee's data
> back into the store that was just purged. Regression tests: `test/session_switch_test.dart`.

**`_safe(key)`** maps a key to a filename, replacing anything outside `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` and
truncating at 120 chars. Because `LiCacheKeys` only ever produces `[A-Za-z0-9_]`, this is an
identity mapping in practice — which is what keeps prefix-matching reliable.

---

### 14.4 `LiCacheKeys` — the map of what is cached

`li_cache_keys.dart` (32 lines). Centralised so the read layer and the optimistic write layer
agree on exactly which file a resource lives in.

| Key / builder | Caches | Prefix constant |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `catalog` = `li_catalog` | The questionnaire | — |
| `linesAll` = `li_lines_all` | The full line list (empty search only) | — |
| `subdivisions` = `li_subdivisions` | Subdivision list | — |
| `towers(lineId)` = `li_towers_<id>` | One line's towers | — |
| `inspections({subdivision, line, tower})` = `li_insp_<s>_<l>_<t>` | Inspection summaries | `li_insp_` |
| `inspectionDetail(id)` = `li_insp_detail_<id>` | One inspection | `li_insp_detail_` |
| `tickets({status, subdivision, line, tower})` = `li_tickets_<st>_<s>_<l>_<t>` | Ticket lists | `li_tickets_` |
| `support({subdivision})` = `li_support_<s>` | Support requests | `li_support_` |
| `dashboard({subdivision})` = `li_dash_<s>` | Home KPIs | — |

`null` renders as the literal `x`, so an unfiltered ticket list is `li_tickets_x_x_x_x`.

> ⚠️ **Prefix collision.** `inspectionDetailPrefix` (`li_insp_detail_`) starts with
> `inspectionsPrefix` (`li_insp_`). Any future `patchCachesWithPrefix(inspectionsPrefix, …)` would
> also rewrite every detail entry. No current caller does this, so it is latent, not live.

---

### 14.5 `OutboxStore` — the durable change queue

`outbox.dart`.

**Every op has an owner.** `OutboxOp.owner` is stamped from
`AuthStore.instance.session?.employeeId` at `enqueue()` time, and `OutboxOp.ownerId` falls back to
the employee id the payload already carries for its type (`inspector_employee_id` / `closed_by` /
`raised_by` / `resolved_by`) so ops queued by a build from before the field still resolve to the
right person instead of being stranded.

| Method | Scope |
| --- | --- |
| `list()` | **The signed-in employee's ops only** — the default, so a new caller is safe by remembering nothing. The drain, the pending badge and the map's "waiting to sync" rings all read this. |
| `listAll()` | Every op regardless of owner. Diagnostics, storage readouts, and `init()`'s sequence seed — which *must* see other employees' files, or it would hand out seqs already on disk and overwrite their work. |

An op whose owner cannot be recovered at all counts as the current session's: `OfflineActions`
always names its author, so the only way to reach that state is a hand-built op, and stranding a
real inspection forever is worse than the residual risk.

> **Fixed — one employee's fieldwork could be recorded against another.** The queue is the one
> thing a sign-out must not throw away, and it had no notion of whose work it held. `SyncEngine`
> drained it with whatever token was current, and the server credits an inspection to the token
> holder (`_create_inspection(request.user.employee_id, …)`, not the payload's
> `inspector_employee_id`) — so an inspection queued offline by an AEE and drained after somebody
> else signed in was attributed to that second person, GPS presence proof included. Ops that do not
> belong to the session are now simply absent from `list()`: never sent, never retried, never
> parked, and visible again the moment their author signs back in. The same filter fixes a smaller
> bug — `SyncEngine.start()` runs from `main()` before any login, and used to drain with no token at
> all, burning one of the eight attempts per pass until real work was parked as permanently failed
> over a 401 that had nothing to do with it. Regression tests: `test/session_switch_test.dart`.

**Four op types** (`OpType`), each mapping to exactly one backend call:
`inspection`, `ticket_close`, `support_create`, `support_resolve`.

**`OutboxOp` fields:**

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Unique id — **and the inspection's `client_id` idempotency key** |
| `seq` | Monotonic counter for FIFO ordering |
| `type` | One of `OpType` |
| `payload` | The JSON body to send |
| `media` | `photo_key → staged file path` (inspections only) |
| `createdAt` | Epoch millis |
| `attempts` | Sync attempts so far |
| `lastError` | Human-readable last failure, shown in the details sheet |
| `failed` | True once attempts are exhausted; kept for visibility, no longer retried |

**One file per op** — `outbox/<seq padded to 12>_<id>.json`. The rationale
(`outbox.dart:102-104`) is that a crash mid-write can damage at most one op, never the whole
queue, and the zero-padded names sort lexically into FIFO order. Writes go through
`.tmp` + `rename`.

`init()` scans the directory and seeds `_nextSeq` from the highest surviving `seq`, so ordering
continues correctly across app restarts.

`remove(op)` deletes both the op file **and its staged photos** — the only place staged media is
cleaned up. Remember that; it matters in §14.11.

---

### 14.6 `SyncEngine` — draining the queue

`sync_engine.dart` (261 lines). Publishes `ValueNotifier<SyncStatus> status` and
`ValueNotifier<int> dataRevision` (bumped on every successful op so open screens can refresh
against now-authoritative data).

**Triggers:** `start()` at app launch; `online` flipping true; `onResume()` when the app
foregrounds; `kick()` after any enqueue; a 30-second retry timer while work remains;
`syncNow()` for an awaited drain.

**Re-entrancy.** `_syncing` guards concurrent drains; `_rerunRequested` records that work arrived
mid-drain so a follow-up pass runs immediately rather than waiting for the timer.

**The three failure policies** — this is the heart of the design, and each differs for a reason:

| Failure | Response | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Transport error** (`SocketException`, `TimeoutException`, `ClientException`, `HandshakeException`) | Stop the pass, `reportFailure()`, break the loop. **`attempts` is not incremented.** | Losing signal is not the record's fault. Burning attempts on it would eventually park perfectly good work as failed |
| **Server rejection** (any other exception) | `attempts++`, store `lastError`, park as `failed` at 8 | A record the server genuinely refuses must not wedge the queue behind it forever |
| **Unknown op type** | Silently return (leaving the op queued) | Forward/backward compatibility with a different build |

```dart
} catch (e) {
  if (_isNetworkError(e)) {
    networkBroke = true;
    ConnectivityService.instance.reportFailure();
    break;                                  // stop the pass, don't punish the op
  }
  op.attempts++;
  op.lastError = _short(e);
  if (op.attempts >= _maxAttempts) op.failed = true;   // _maxAttempts = 8
  await OutboxStore.instance.update(op);
}
```

Note the loop also re-checks `ConnectivityService.online` before each op and skips ops already
marked `failed`.

---

### 14.7 Idempotency end-to-end — the most important correctness property

If you understand one thing about this subsystem, make it this.

1. When the inspector taps Save, the form generates **one** `client_id` — an RFC-4122 v4 UUID
   from `Random.secure()` (`utils/uuid.dart`).
2. That UUID becomes the outbox op's `id` (`enqueue(..., id: clientId)`).
3. Every sync attempt sends **the same** `client_id` (`submitInspection(clientId: op.id)`).
4. Server-side, `Inspection.client_id` is `unique`, and both create endpoints check it before
   inserting: an existing record returns **200 with the existing row**, a new one returns **201**
   (§11).
5. The op is only removed from the outbox after a 2xx.

The failure this defends against is the nasty one: **the request succeeded but the response was
lost.** The server saved the inspection; the phone saw a timeout. On retry the server recognises
the replay and returns 200 instead of creating a second inspection — and a second set of defect
tickets.

The other three op types are idempotent by nature:

| Op | Why replay is safe |
| --- | --- |
| `ticket_close` | Closing a closed ticket returns the ticket unchanged (`DefectTicketCloseView` early-returns when `status == 'closed'`) |
| `support_resolve` | Resolving sets the same fields to the same values |
| `support_create` | Server-side content dedup: an open request with identical subject+text from the same employee returns 200 rather than duplicating |

---

### 14.8 `OfflineActions` — the optimistic write layer

`offline_actions.dart` (427 lines). Screens never call the API directly for writes; they call
this, which guarantees durability and immediate visible feedback.

**`saveInspection(...)` — four steps:**

1. **Stage photos.** Each picked photo is copied into `media/` as
   `<clientId>_<photoKey><ext>`, out of the evictable picker cache.
2. **Enqueue** with `id: clientId`. The payload carries the submit fields plus display-only
   metadata (`tower_number`, `line_name`, `worst`, `defect_count`) that the create view ignores
   but the optimistic UI needs.
3. **Insert optimistic rows** so the inspection appears in History and on the map instantly, with
   no signal:
   - a summary prepended to `li_insp_<line>` with `'_pending': true`
   - a full synthetic detail cached under `li_insp_detail_<negId>`, reconstructed from the
     catalog so item and defect *labels* render offline
   - photos referenced as `local://<path>` so the detail viewer can render them from disk before
     upload
4. **Drain if online** (`syncNow()`), then check whether the op is gone from the outbox. If it
   synced, the optimistic rows are removed so a later offline read cannot show a duplicate
   alongside the authoritative record.

**The negative-id convention.** `negId = -op.createdAt` — a negative id marks a row that exists
only locally. `LineInspectionApi.loadInspectionDetail` special-cases `id < 0` and reads straight
from the cache, never attempting a network call. Synthetic child rows count down from `-1`.

> Minor: two inspections saved in the *same millisecond* would collide on `negId`. Not reachable
> at human tapping speed, but it is a timestamp, not a guaranteed-unique id.

**Ticket and support writes** take the opposite default — try live first when online, fall back to
the queue **only on a transport error**:

```dart
} catch (e) {
  if (!_isNetworkError(e)) rethrow;   // a real server rejection surfaces to the user
}
```

This asymmetry is correct. An inspection represents irreplaceable field work and must be captured
durably before anything else. A ticket close is cheap to repeat and the user is better served by
an immediate error than by a silent queue.

---

### 14.9 `OfflineDownloader` — "Download my area"

`offline_download.dart` (187 lines). Pre-warms everything needed to inspect with no signal.

Four phases, reported through `DownloadProgress {phase, done, total, bytes}`:

| Phase | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `lines` | `searchLines('')` — all lines in scope (cache-through, so it warms `li_lines_all`) |
| `towers` | Per line: `towersForLine()` + `loadInspections(line:)`, warming `li_towers_<id>` and collecting coordinates |
| `catalog` | `loadCatalog()` so the form opens offline |
| `tiles` | Every OSM tile over the bounding box of all collected towers, **pinned** |

**Tile maths.** Standard slippy-tile projection, zooms **11–16** ("corridor overview" through
"standing at the tower"), bbox padded by 0.01° (~1 km) so corridor edges aren't clipped, capped
at `_maxTiles = 20000`.

A per-line failure is swallowed so one bad line doesn't abort the whole download. `cancel()` sets
a flag checked between items.

> ⚠️ **Three findings here.**
>
> 1. **`estimateTiles()` duplicates the entire crawl.** `_assignedBbox()` re-fetches every line
>    *and every line's towers* purely to compute a bounding box for the size preview — then
>    `downloadJurisdiction()` fetches them all again. On a large jurisdiction that is two full
>    passes over the API before a single tile is downloaded.
> 2. **The 20,000-tile cap truncates silently.** The comment at `offline_download.dart:39-41`
>    says it is "surfaced to the user if hit", but `_tilesFor` simply `return`s early and the
>    returned count is indistinguishable from a complete download. An engineer with a large
>    jurisdiction would believe their whole area was downloaded when the outer zooms were dropped.
> 3. **Bulk-downloading OSM tiles violates the OSM Tile Usage Policy.** Up to 20,000 tiles per
>    user per download from `tile.openstreetmap.org` is exactly the bulk-download case that
>    policy prohibits, and the User-Agent is a bare package name. For production this needs a
>    self-hosted tile server or a commercial provider. This is an operational/compliance risk, not
>    just a nicety.

---

### 14.10 `TileCache` — disk cache with a pinned region

`tile_cache.dart` (225 lines). Implements `flutter_map`'s `TileProvider`, so caching is invisible
to the map widget.

**Read order:** `pinned/` → LRU `tiles/` (touch `mtime` for LRU) → network (12 s timeout) → write
to LRU → return. `_inFlight` de-duplicates concurrent requests for the same URL.

**LRU:** soft cap `160 MB`, pruned back to **80%** (128 MB) oldest-first, triggered every 200
writes rather than on every write.

**Pinning is what makes "Download my area" trustworthy.** Pinned tiles live in `tiles/pinned/`,
and `_prune()` enumerates only `_dir` non-recursively while filtering `e is File`, so the pinned
subdirectory is never scanned and never evicted. Without this, a 150 MB region download would
promptly evict itself through normal map panning. `pinnedBytes()` and `clearPinned()` let the UI
report and reclaim the space.

> ⚠️ **Finding: 32-bit tile-URL hashing risks visible collisions.** Filenames come from
> `_hash()`, an FNV-1a **32-bit** hash. By the birthday bound, expected collisions ≈ n²/2³³:
> at 20,000 tiles ≈ **4.7%** chance of at least one collision; at 50,000 tiles (a pinned region
> plus normal browsing) ≈ **29%**. A collision means one tile's image is served in place of
> another — a wrong patch of map, silently, with no error. Widening to a 64-bit hash (or SHA-1
> truncated to 16 hex chars) removes the risk for a one-line change.

---

### 14.11 `LineInspectionApi` — the transport

`line_inspection_api.dart` (461 lines). Every read goes through one core:

```dart
static Future<String> _readThrough(String key, Future<String> Function() fetch,
                                   {String what = 'this data'}) async {
  if (ConnectivityService.instance.online.value) {
    try {
      final body = await fetch();
      await LocalStore.instance.putCache(key, body);   // write-through
      return body;
    } catch (e) {
      if (_isNetworkError(e)) ConnectivityService.instance.reportFailure();
      final cached = await LocalStore.instance.getCache(key);
      if (cached != null) return cached;               // prefer stale over error
      rethrow;
    }
  }
  final cached = await LocalStore.instance.getCache(key);
  if (cached != null) return cached;
  throw OfflineNoCacheException(what);                 // friendly, actionable
}
```

Note the policy in the catch: **prefer showing saved data over showing an error**, and only
surface the error when there is nothing cached. `OfflineNoCacheException` renders as
*"You're offline and \<what\> hasn't been saved on this device yet. Connect to the internet once
to load it."*

| Method | Endpoint | Cache key | Offline behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `login` | `POST /auth/login/` | — | Online only; 401 ⇒ `LoginFailedException` |
| `logout` | `POST /auth/logout/` | — | Best-effort; local clear is what matters |
| `loadCatalog` | `GET /catalog/` | `li_catalog` | Cached |
| `cachedCatalog` | — | `li_catalog` | Cache-only, never hits network |
| `searchLines` | `GET /lines/?search=` | `li_lines_all` | **Special**: only the empty query is cached; offline searches filter the cached full list locally |
| `towersForLine` | `GET /lines/<id>/towers/` | `li_towers_<id>` | Cached |
| `loadSubdivisions` | `GET /subdivisions/` | `li_subdivisions` | Cached |
| `loadInspections` | `GET /line-inspections/list/` | `li_insp_…` | Cached |
| `loadInspectionDetail` | `GET /line-inspections/<id>/` | `li_insp_detail_<id>` | Cached; `id < 0` ⇒ cache-only |
| `loadTickets` | `GET /tickets/` | `li_tickets_…` | Cached |
| `loadSupportRequests` | `GET /support-requests/` | `li_support_…` | Cached |
| `loadDashboard` | `GET /dashboard/` | `li_dash_…` | Cached (30 s timeout) |
| `closeTicket` | `POST /tickets/<id>/close/` | — | Write — via outbox |
| `createSupportRequest` | `POST /support-requests/` | — | Write — via outbox |
| `resolveSupportRequest` | `POST /support-requests/<id>/resolve/` | — | Write — via outbox |
| `submitInspection` | `POST /line-inspections/` | — | Write — via outbox |

**`_guard(res)`** raises `UnauthorizedException` on any 401, which the UI turns into a return to
the login screen. **`mediaUrl(path)`** derives the media host by stripping a trailing `/api` from
the base URL — the app's own fallback for building absolute photo URLs.

**`submitInspection`** builds the multipart body: one `payload` text field holding the whole
inspection as JSON, plus one file part per `photo_key`. Its timeout **scales with payload size** —
`40 + 20 × photoCount` seconds — because a 10-photo inspection over 2G is genuinely slow.

> ⚠️ **Finding: `submitInspection` never sends `inspection_type`.** The payload
> (`line_inspection_api.dart:433-446`) has no such key, and no `.dart` file mentions
> `ground_patrol` or `pmi`. Every mobile inspection therefore lands with
> `Inspection.inspection_type = NULL`, so the Ground-Patrol/PMI cycle filters on the register,
> the map and the dashboard match nothing. Corroborates the §6 finding — this is the single
> highest-impact functional gap found in the app.

---

### 14.12 `SyncStatusBar` — what the user sees

`sync_status_bar.dart` (274 lines). A slim banner above the tab content, driven by
`SyncEngine.status`:

| State | Banner |
| --- | --- |
| Online, nothing queued | *(hidden)* |
| Syncing | Progress indicator |
| Offline | "Offline — showing saved data" · action **Details** when work is queued |
| Failed ops present | Red: "N changes didn't sync" · action **Retry** |
| Pending only | Blue: "N changes to upload" · action **Sync now** |

Tapping opens a details sheet listing each op by `label` (e.g. *"Inspection · Tower 127"*) with
its state — `Waiting to retry (attempts)` or the error for failed ops.

> 🔴 **Finding (significant): the "Retry" action on failed ops does nothing.**
>
> The banner offers **Retry** when `failed > 0`, and the sheet's button calls
> `SyncEngine.syncNow()` → `_drain()`. But the drain loop begins with:
>
> ```dart
> for (final op in ops) {
>   if (op.failed) continue;      // ← failed ops are skipped, always
> ```
>
> and **nothing anywhere in the codebase ever resets `failed` back to `false`** (verified by
> grepping `lib/` for `failed = false`). So the Retry affordance kicks a drain that skips exactly
> the ops the user is trying to retry. There is also no discard action.
>
> **Consequences.** An inspection that hits 8 non-transport rejections is permanently stranded:
> it cannot be retried, cannot be deleted, stays in the banner forever, and its staged photos are
> never cleaned up (`remove()` — the only caller of `deleteMedia` — runs only on success), so it
> leaks disk indefinitely.
>
> **How a good record gets stranded.** A 401 is *not* a network error, so it increments
> `attempts`. If the mobile token expires or is revoked while the engineer is offline, the next
> time they regain signal the drain fires up to 8 times in quick succession, all 401, and parks
> genuine field work as permanently failed before the user has any chance to re-login.
>
> **Suggested fix (small):** treat 401 like a transport error (pause the drain, don't increment)
> and add a "Retry failed" action that sets `failed = false; attempts = 0` and re-drains, plus a
> discard action that calls `OutboxStore.remove`.

---

### 14.13 Failure-mode walkthroughs

**(a) Captured with no signal; app killed; phone rebooted; signal returns two days later.**
Photos are staged into `media/` and the op is written to `outbox/` before Save returns, both under
the non-evictable support directory. Optimistic rows make the inspection visible in History
immediately, flagged `_pending`. Reboot loses nothing; `OutboxStore.init()` re-seeds the sequence
from disk and `SyncEngine.start()` attempts a drain. Two days later, `connectivity_plus` reports
a link, the `/ping/` probe succeeds, `online` flips true, the drain runs, the inspection uploads
with its original `client_id`, tickets are raised server-side, the op and its photos are deleted,
and `dataRevision` bumps so open screens refresh. **Nothing is lost.**

**(b) Submit sent, response lost mid-flight.** The server committed; the phone saw a timeout —
a transport error, so the pass stops and `attempts` is *not* incremented. On the next drain the
same `client_id` is sent, the server recognises the replay and returns **200** with the existing
record, and the op is removed. **No duplicate inspection, no duplicate tickets.**

**(c) Server rejects a submit — tower outside the engineer's jurisdiction.** `can_edit_tower`
fails and DRF returns **403**. Not a transport error, so `attempts` increments and the op stays
queued with `lastError` visible in the details sheet. After 8 passes it parks as `failed`. Because
403 is deterministic, those 8 retries are pure waste — and then §14.12 applies: the work can never
be retried or discarded from the app. This is the case where the retry bug hurts most, because it
looks identical to a transient failure to the user.

**(d) Token expired while offline.** Reads served from cache keep working, so nothing looks
wrong. On reconnect, queued writes get 401 → `UnauthorizedException`. Interactive reads surface it
and the app returns to login. But drained ops treat it as a server rejection: up to 8 attempts,
then permanently failed — see the finding above. **This is the most likely real-world path to
losing field work**, because the 30-day token expiry and multi-day offline stints are exactly the
intended usage pattern.

---

### 14.14 Findings summary for this section

| # | Finding | Location | Severity |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **"Retry" on failed ops is a no-op**; `failed` is never reset, no discard action; stranded work is unrecoverable and leaks staged photos | `sync_engine.dart:137`, `sync_status_bar.dart:99` | **High** |
| 2 | **401 counts as a server rejection**, so an expired token during an offline stint can permanently park good inspections | `sync_engine.dart:144-154` | **High** |
| 3 | **`inspection_type` is never sent**, so every mobile inspection is NULL and all Ground-Patrol/PMI filtering is inert | `line_inspection_api.dart:433-446` | **High** |
| 4 | **32-bit FNV-1a tile hashing** — ~29% collision probability at 50k tiles ⇒ wrong map imagery, silently | `tile_cache.dart:216` | Medium |
| 5 | **Bulk OSM tile download** (up to 20k/user) violates the OSM Tile Usage Policy | `offline_download.dart:35,41` | Medium (compliance) |
| 6 | **Tile cap truncates silently** despite a comment claiming it is surfaced | `offline_download.dart:181` | Medium |
| 7 | **`estimateTiles()` duplicates the whole line+tower crawl** before the download repeats it | `offline_download.dart:122-138` | Low (perf) |
| 8 | **No cache eviction** — `cache/` has no size cap or TTL | `local_store.dart` | Low |
| 9 | **`li_insp_detail_` is a prefix-subset of `li_insp_`** — latent hazard for future `patchCachesWithPrefix` callers | `li_cache_keys.dart:16,20` | Low (latent) |
| 10 | **`negId` derives from a millisecond timestamp**, not a guaranteed-unique value | `offline_actions.dart:94` | Very low |

Set against these, the subsystem gets the hard parts right: durability before acknowledgement,
atomic writes, correct end-to-end idempotency, a genuine reachability probe rather than a
link check, non-evictable storage for field work, and pinned tiles that survive LRU pressure.
The defects above are all in the *recovery* paths, not the happy path.

A note on the verification claims: "31 checks" and "43 checks" refer to *manual transactional

reproducible from this checkout — see §15.3.

### 15.2 Design pivots and bugs caught — institutional memory

The most valuable thing in the README's changelog is the reasoning. These are decisions a future
maintainer would otherwise re-litigate or accidentally undo.

**The accidental `gisapp` dependency (Phase 1 → 1.5).** Phase 1 imported the ArcGIS client from a
sibling app. That silently made `line_inspection` undeployable on servers that don't install
`gisapp`. The fix was to **copy** `arcgis_client.py` (and later the Keycloak client) into
`line_inspection/services/`. The duplication is a deliberate, documented trade for deployment
independence — with a standing obligation to port fixes by hand in both directions. That this
worked is visible in `transcoapps/settings.py:82-88`, where every sibling app is commented out and
the project still runs.

**The Keycloak pivot (post-Phase 2).** Two separate discoveries, in order: (1) the realm name the
team had been given, `aptransco-realm`, **does not exist** — the real realm is `APTRANSCO-EMP`;
(2) once that was corrected, Keycloak still rejected the `redirect_uri` because it was never
registered on the `clear` client, which requires admin-console access the team doesn't have. So
Keycloak was left fully built but dormant, and login switched to the legacy checkCred gateway.
`keycloak_client.py` was deliberately never touched — only ~15 lines of view glue were removed —
so re-enabling it later is a small change. The re-enable recipe is in §3.

**The SAP auto-match threshold (Phase 2).** Initially 0.5 Jaccard similarity. Spot-checking found
false positives on line names sharing only a voltage and circuit-number token (e.g. two unrelated
"220KV … Ckt-1" lines). Raised to **0.75**, which is why only 302 of 1,212 lines auto-mapped —
the remaining 75% are queued for manual review rather than wrongly linked. **Do not lower this
threshold to improve the mapping rate**; that is the mistake it was raised to prevent.

**Ticket close locked out Admins (Phase 2).** The first implementation checked only the
requester's own jurisdiction, which incorrectly blocked Admins acting in oversight over
jurisdiction they had themselves assigned to others. Fixed by adding an `is_admin` branch — though
see F-2 in §15.4: the fix over-corrected into a *global* admin check with no oversight narrowing.

**`Line.sap_line` uniqueness and the PK choice.** A nullable unique FK (later `OneToOneField`)
allows unlimited unmapped lines while forbidding double-mapping. The surrogate `id` was kept as PK
rather than adopting the SAP functional location, because a PK cannot be NULL during a long manual
mapping effort, SAP codes get corrected, lines get LILO-split, and a mutable PK would cascade
through ~113k `Tower.line` rows and the `RoleAssignment.lines` M2M.

**One Tower table, not three.** ~113k rows including VT is small for Postgres, and splitting by
voltage would have broken the `Inspection`/`DefectTicket` foreign keys for no measurable gain.

**LILO revive-in-place.** The insight worth preserving: when ArcGIS delete-recreates a LILO'd line,
every `arcgis_object_id` churns, but the *physical towers do not move*. Coordinates are therefore
the durable identity. Survivors are re-identified by coordinates and revived under their original
PK, so inspection history, schedule position and range assignments all survive an event that would
otherwise strand them.

### 15.3 Testing — the honest state

**Python: one test module, which cannot run as shipped.**

`line_inspection/tests/test_dashboard.py` (444 lines) contains **8 test classes / 26 test methods**:

| Class | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| `DashboardScopeTests` (9 tests) | Oversight widening, edit-scope isolation, functional tiers, status cache + `inspection_type`, rollup counts, reports gating, **map bbox security**, register matrix + export, register line-scope 403 |
| `TowerScheduleProjectionTests` (2) | Geometry vertex extraction and projection ordering (`SimpleTestCase` — no DB) |
| `RegisterVTCompletenessTests` (1) | VT columns sourcing status from the co-located real tower |
| `FromToRangeTests` (2) | Ranges restricting jurisdiction; supervisor oversight unioning ranges |
| `TowerInspectionHistoryTests` (3) | History ordering + defect count, per-tower drill-down render, cycle filter + out-of-scope |
| `LiloReconcileTests` (4) | Proposal classification, history-preserving apply, churn detection, super-admin gating |
| `CircuitParseTests` (2) | `_parse_circuit_count`, structure linking by co-location |
| `TowerStructureTests` (4) | Scopes exclude VT, `circuits_at`, register lists real only, **VT inspection rejected** |

The blocker is stated in the module's own header:

> *"line_inspection models are routed to the `line_inspection_db` Postgres connection (the `clear`
> schema) and the status helper uses Postgres `DISTINCT ON`, so these tests require a Postgres test
> database for that connection — they will not run on the default sqlite alias."*

Six of the eight classes declare `databases = {'default', 'line_inspection_db'}`, so Django manages
transactions on both connections.

**To actually run them today** you need a Postgres instance the test runner can create a
`test_<name>` database on, with the `clear` schema available, and `PG_*` pointing at it:

```bash
# Both aliases point at the same server, so one Postgres is enough.
python manage.py test line_inspection --keepdb
```

`--keepdb` is worth using: creating the schema and running eight migrations per run is slow.
Note that the test database still needs the `clear` schema to exist — the router's
`search_path=clear` is not created by `migrate` itself.

**What is not covered at all:** the entire REST API surface (no test touches
`api/views.py` except `_create_inspection` indirectly), authentication and the three DRF auth
classes, `MobileAuthToken`, the GPS presence gate, the multipart submit path, `client_id`
idempotency, the admin panel's CRUD screens, the services layer (ArcGIS/SAP/checkCred/Keycloak
clients), and every management command except the two `sync_gis_towers` helpers.

**Flutter: two tests, both trivial.** `test/widget_test.dart` is a smoke test asserting the app
boots and renders a `MaterialApp`; `test/uuid_test.dart` checks UUID v4 formatting. There is no
test of the outbox, the sync engine, the cache layer, or the form. `flutter analyze` is reported
clean.

**No CI.** There is no workflow file, no `tox.ini`, no pre-commit config anywhere in the tree.
Nothing runs any of this automatically.

### 15.5 Recommended next steps

Ordered by value-per-effort, not by section order.

1. **Rotate the Keycloak secret and move all four literals to `.env.local`** (gaps 1–3). One
   commit. Until this is done nothing else matters, because the credential is already exposed.
2. **Fix the two authorization holes** (gaps 4–5). Roughly ten lines: add an `is_admin` +
   oversight check to `SupportRequestResolveView`, and narrow the ticket-close admin branch to the
   caller's oversight scope. These are the only places where the otherwise-careful scoping model
   is actually broken.
3. **Send `inspection_type` from the app** (gap 7). Add a cycle selector to the form and one key
   to the submit payload. This single field switches on register cycles, map cycle filters and
   dashboard splits — the highest functional return in the list.
4. **Fix the sync recovery paths** (gaps 8–9). Treat 401 as a pause-not-punish condition, and make
   Retry actually reset `failed`/`attempts`. This is the difference between "the app occasionally
   fails to sync" and "the app occasionally destroys a day of field work".
5. **Stand up a Postgres CI database and run the existing 26 tests** (§15.3). The tests already
   exist and already encode the security invariants; they simply never run. Then extend to the API
   surface, which currently has none.
6. **Reconcile the two criticality engines** (gap 10). Pick the server's operator set as
   canonical, implement it exactly in Dart, and add a shared fixture both sides evaluate.
7. **Close the GPS bypass** (gap 11) by routing the History tab's inspect action through
   `launchInspection`.
8. **Fix `applicable_tower_types` through the checklist editor** (gap 14) using the real observed
   `Tower.tower_type` values. No deploy needed — this is a data fix, and the editor already
   surfaces the real values as checkboxes.
9. **Production settings** (`DEBUG=False`, real `ALLOWED_HOSTS`, static/media behind nginx,
   a real tile source instead of bulk OSM, self-hosted Leaflet). This is Phase 5's stated scope.
10. **Delete the dead weight** (gaps 32–36). Low value individually, but it removes the standing
    confusion about which backend and which data are real.

### 15.6 The donor / reference project

`Aptransco_TIS-main/` is a complete, working system built by a different team, included in this
repository as **a specification and a client — never a dependency**.

| Part | What it is | Status here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `drone_inspection_app/` | An offline-first Flutter field app | **LIVE.** Edited in place and re-homed onto this backend in Phase 4 |
| `aptransco_backend/` | A thin, auth-less DRF backend: `managed=False` models mirroring the `clear` schema, plus an older legacy `inspections` app on SQLite | **DEAD.** Contract spec only |
| `README.md` | The donor's setup/integration guide, incl. "Using the app with your OWN backend" (the API contract) | **DELETED** from the tree during this document's authoring — noted here only so references to it elsewhere make sense |
| `project.md` | The donor's file-by-file internals reference | **DELETED** likewise |

**What was taken:** the API contract and the patterns — a fully data-driven questionnaire rendered
from `GET /catalog/`, `client_id` idempotency, the durable offline outbox, atomic multi-photo
create, and thumbnailing.

**What was explicitly not reused:** the backend code itself, and its older `inspections` app,
which used flat SQLite rows with free-text `component`/`defect` strings — the very thing the
editable catalog with follow-up questions and criticality rules replaces.

**Why the app was edited in place rather than rewritten:** it was already a working, field-tested
offline-first client. Phase 4 replaced its backend, added real authentication, added the GPS gate
and the five-tab shell, and left the offline machinery — the genuinely hard part — intact.

The donor backend's `line_inspection` app is a useful read for exactly one purpose: it shows the
minimal read/write surface the Flutter app depends on. Beyond that, ignore it. Its
`settings.py:120` also carries the same hardcoded `subhash` database password noted in §2.7.

### 15.7 Glossary

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| **AEE** | Assistant Executive Engineer. SAP codes `AAE`/`AE`. The cadre that performs field inspections |
| **ADE / DEE** | (Assistant) Deputy Executive Engineer. SAP code `ADE/AEE`. Also performs inspections |
| **APTRANSCO** | Transmission Corporation of Andhra Pradesh — the state transmission utility that owns this system |
| **ArcGIS** | Esri's GIS platform. APTRANSCO's portal is the **system of record** for all tower/line/substation master data |
| **bundle** | Multiple physical conductors per electrical phase (`no_of_conductors_per_phase`). Distinct from circuit count |
| **cadre** | SAP employee grade (`emp_sub_grp`). Codes are coarse and combined — `DE/EE` is **one** code — which is why authorization never derives from cadre |
| **catalog version** | A singleton counter bumped on every questionnaire change and stamped onto each `Inspection`, so historical records stay traceable to the catalog shape that produced them |
| **CE** | Chief Engineer. Management cadre — sees the zonal/circle/division rollups |
| **checkCred** | APTRANSCO's legacy employee-credential HTTP gateway (`qaserv.aptransco.co.in/qath`). The **active** authentication mechanism for both web and mobile |
| **circle** | Administrative tier between zone and division |
| **circuit** | One electrical three-phase set. A single physical structure may carry 1, 2 or 4 circuits |
| **CMD / JMD / GM / Director** | Top management cadres. Members of `MANAGEMENT_SUBGRPS`, which gates the rollup dashboards |
| **CP / SP** | `Tower.cp_sp` — the structure's corridor role (Cutting Point / Suspension Point, also `Boom`). Display and QA only |
| **criticality** | Defect severity: `minor` / `major` / `critical`. Tower *status* adds `ok` (inspected, clean) and `none` (never inspected) |
| **DefectEntry** | One recorded defect inside an inspection, with its follow-up answers, suggested and confirmed criticality, note and photo |
| **DefectTicket** | The actionable work item auto-raised from each `DefectEntry`, with labels snapshotted so it stays readable if the catalog wording changes |
| **division** | Administrative tier between circle and subdivision |
| **EE** | Executive Engineer. SAP code `DE/EE`. The **Admin** tier — assigns jurisdiction to Users |
| **EHT** | Extra High Tension — the 132/220/400 kV voltage classes in scope |
| **emp_sub_grp** | The SAP field holding the cadre code. Used **only** for display labels and the management gate |
| **functional location** | SAP's asset identifier for a line. The natural key of `SapLine` |
| **Ground Patrolling** | The routine, non-detailed half of the twice-yearly inspection cycle |
| **jurisdiction** | The set of towers an employee may **inspect and edit**, from their own `RoleAssignment` and `LineTowerAssignment` rows only. `jurisdiction.py` |
| **Keycloak** | The OIDC identity provider, realm `APTRANSCO-EMP`. Fully built but **dormant** — the redirect URI was never registered |
| **LILO** | *Loop-In Loop-Out* — cutting an existing line to loop it into a new substation, splitting one line into two or more. ~20–30/year, Super-Admin only |
| **line** | A transmission circuit between two substations, carrying a sequence of towers |
| **line_sequence** | A tower's ordinal position along its line, computed by projecting its geometry onto the line polyline. Backbone of range assignments and register column order |
| **outbox** | The Flutter app's durable, file-per-op FIFO queue of changes made offline |
| **oversight** | The set of towers an employee may **view**: their own jurisdiction ∪ everyone below them in the SAP reporting tree. **Read-only** — never grants edit rights. `viewing.py` |
| **PMI** | Pre-Monsoon Inspection — the detailed half of the twice-yearly cycle, done before the monsoon |
| **position id** | The SAP identifier for a *post* (not a person). Admin rights are granted to positions via `FieldEECadrePosition`, so they follow the post through staff changes |
| **presence flag** | The GPS proof-of-presence outcome on an inspection: `in_range` (≤ 50 m), `out_of_range`, or `no_fix`. The latter two require an audited override reason |
| **register** | The formal per-line patrolling record — a checklist-item × tower matrix. A digital replica of the paper field register, with Print and Excel export |
| **RFC** | SAP's Remote Function Call. Reached here over an HTTP REST adapter |
| **RoleAssignment** | A grant of a subdivision and/or specific lines to an employee. The basis of jurisdiction |
| **SAP** | APTRANSCO's ERP. Source of employee/cadre master data and of line functional locations |
| **SE** | Superintending Engineer. Supervisory tier above EE |
| **span** | The conductor run between two adjacent towers. `Tower.span_km` is only reliably populated on 132 kV |
| **structure_key** | A coordinate-derived key grouping a real tower and all its co-located VT rows into one **physical structure**. The join key for `circuits_at()` and for the register's VT columns |
| **subdivision** | The smallest administrative unit — the usual jurisdiction granularity |
| **substation** | A switching/transformation site terminating one or more lines |
| **Super Admin** | The tier that decides who is an Admin. Bootstrapped only via `manage.py grant_super_admin`, because an empty permissions table would otherwise lock everyone out |
| **tower** | One structure carrying the conductors. The unit of inspection |
| **tower schedule** | The ordered list of towers along a line, by `line_sequence` |
| **tower type** | `Tower.tower_type` from ArcGIS (e.g. `"Boom"`). The checklist's `applicable_tower_types` gate still holds POC placeholders instead — see gap 14 |
| **VT / virtual tower** | An extra ArcGIS row representing an additional circuit on an existing physical structure, co-located with the real tower. `is_virtual=True`. **Never inspected or counted** — VT rows exist so each circuit's line has a complete tower column |
| **zone** | The largest administrative tier |
